53:1: Interpretation of Surat An-Najm Al-Bukhari said: Nasr bin Ali told us, Abu Ahmad told me - meaning Al-Zubaidi - Israel told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Al-Aswad bin Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The first Surah in which a prostration was revealed was Al-Najm. He said: So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated, and those behind him prostrated, except for a man whom I saw take a handful of dirt and prostrate on it. I saw him after that being killed as a disbeliever, and he was Umayyah bin Khalaf. Al-Bukhari also narrated it in several places, as did Muslim, Abu Dawud, and Al-Nasa’i through various chains of transmission on the authority of Abu Ishaq. His saying in Al-Mumta’a that it is Umayyah bin Khalaf in this narration is problematic, because it has been narrated through other chains of transmission that it is Utbah bin Rabi’ah. In the name of God, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful Al-Sha'bi and others said: The Creator swears by whatever He wills of His creation, and the creation should not swear except by the Creator. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim. The commentators differed over the meaning of His statement: And the star when it goes down. Ibn Abi Nujayh said on the authority of Mujahid: He means by the star the Pleiades when it sets with the dawn. This was also narrated on the authority of Ibn Abbas and Sufyan al-Thawri, and Ibn Jarir chose it. Al-Suddi claimed that it was Venus. Ad-Dahhak said: And the star when it goes down when the devils throw it at him. This statement has a direction. Al-A'mash narrated on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the words of God the Almighty: And the star when it goes down, meaning the Qur'an when it is sent down. This verse is like the words of God the Almighty: "So I swear by the positions of the stars. And indeed, it is a great oath, if you but knew. Indeed, it is a noble Qur'an. In a protected Book. None touches it except the purified. A revelation from the Lord of the worlds." And the words of God the Almighty: Your companion has neither strayed nor has he gone astray. This is what is sworn by, and it is the testimony for the Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he is a rightly guided follower of the truth and not astray. He is the ignorant one who takes a path other than the path without knowledge, and the one who goes astray is the one who knows the truth but intentionally turns away from it to something else. So God exonerated His Messenger and His law from resembling the people of misguidance, such as the Christians and the ways of the Jews. It is knowing something and concealing it, and acting in opposition to it. Rather, he, may the peace and blessings of God be upon him, and what he was sent with of the great Shari’ah is the utmost in uprightness, moderation and correctness. For this reason, God the Almighty said: Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination, meaning he does not say a word out of inclination and purpose. It is only a revelation revealed, meaning he only says what he has been commanded to convey to the people in full and complete, without addition or subtraction, as Imam Ahmad narrated: Yazid told us, Jarir ibn Uthman told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Maysarah, on the authority of Abu Umamah, that he heard the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, say: Those who enter Paradise through the intercession of a man who is not a prophet will be like the two tribes - or like one of the two tribes - Rabi’ah and Mudar. A man said: O Messenger of God, is Rabi’ah not from Mudar? He said: I only say what I say. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya bin Saeed narrated to us from Ubaidullah bin Al-Akhns, Al-Walid bin Abdullah narrated to us from Yusuf bin Mahak from Abdullah bin Amr who said: I used to write down everything I heard from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) in order to memorize it, but the Quraysh forbade me, saying: You write down everything you hear from the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) is a human being who speaks in anger. So I stopped writing and mentioned that to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), and he said: Write, for by the One in Whose hand is my soul, nothing comes out of me except the truth. Abu Dawud narrated it from Musaddad and Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, both of them from Yahya bin Saeed Al-Qattan with it. Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ahmad ibn Mansur told us, Abdullah ibn Salih told us, al-Layth told us, on the authority of Ibn Ajlan, on the authority of Zayd ibn Aslam, on the authority of Abu Salih, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: What I have told you is from God, then there is no doubt about it. Then he said: We do not know of it being narrated except with this chain of transmission. Imam Ahmad said: Yunus told us, Layth told us, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Sa’id ibn Abi Sa’id, on the authority of Abu Hurairah, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: I do not say anything but the truth. Some of his companions said: So you joke with us, O Messenger of God? He said: I do not say anything but the truth.

53:5: God the Almighty says, informing about His servant and Messenger Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that the knowledge he brought to the people was strong in strength, that is, Gabriel, peace be upon him, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, it is the word of an honored Messenger, * Possessor of strength with the Lord of the Throne, firmly established, * Obeyed and trustworthy. And He said here, of great stature, meaning of great strength, as stated by Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Abbas said: of good looks. Qatadah said: of tall, handsome character. There is no contradiction between the two statements, as he, peace be upon him, was of good looks and great strength. It was reported in the authentic hadith narrated by Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Charity is not permissible for a rich person or one of good looks. And God the Almighty’s statement: then he rose up means Gabriel, peace be upon him, as stated by Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas. And he was at the highest horizon, that is, Gabriel rose up at the highest horizon, as stated by Ikrimah and others. Ikrimah said: and the highest horizon is from which dawn comes. Mujahid said: it is the place where the sun rises. Qatada said: It is the one from which the day comes, and Ibn Zayd and others said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Masraf bin Amr al-Yami Abu al-Qasim told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Muhammad bin Talha bin Masraf told us, my father told me, on the authority of al-Walid - he is Ibn Qais - on the authority of Ishaq bin Abi al-Kahtalah - I think he mentioned it on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud - that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not see Gabriel in his true form except twice: As for the first time, he asked him to see him in his true form, so the horizon was blocked. And as for the second, he was with him where he ascended, so that is his saying: And he is on the highest horizon. Ibn Jarir said here a saying that I have not seen from anyone else, nor did he narrate it from anyone. The gist of it is that he went to the meaning that he and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were leveled, that is, they were both leveled on the highest horizon, and that was on the night of the Isra’. This is what he said, and no one agreed with him on that. Then he began to explain what he said from the Arabic perspective, so he said: It is like his saying: When we and our fathers were dust, so he connected with fathers to the one referred to in we without making we clear. So is his saying that he was leveled and he. Al-Farra’ mentioned on the authority of some Arabs that he recited to him: Have you not seen that the spring hardens and becomes uneven? And the castor oil that is split This is what he said from the Arabic perspective, but the meaning does not support it, because this vision of Gabriel did not take place on the night of the Isra’, but rather before it, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on earth, so Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended to him and approached him while he was in the form in which God created him, with six hundred wings. Then he saw him after that another descent at the Lote Tree of the Limit, meaning the night of the Isra’. This first vision was in the beginning of the mission after Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him the first time, and God revealed to him the beginning of Surat Al-Iqra’. Then the revelation stopped for a period during which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went repeatedly to throw himself down from the tops of mountains. Whenever he was about to do that, Gabriel called out to him from the air, O Muhammad, you are truly the Messenger of God and I am Gabriel. This calmed him down and made him happy. Whenever the matter took longer, he returned to the same state until Gabriel and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared to him in Al-Abtah in the form in which God created him, with six hundred wings and the greatness of his creation filling the horizon. He approached him and revealed to him from God Almighty what He had commanded him to do. At that point, he knew the greatness of the angel who had come to him with the message and the majesty of his status and the loftiness of his position with his Creator who had sent him to him. As for the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar in his Musnad, where he said: Salamah bin Shabib narrated to us, Saeed bin Mansour narrated to us, Al-Harith bin Ubaid narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Joni, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “While I was sitting, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came and poked me between my shoulders. I went to a tree in which were the nests of birds. He sat in one of them, and I sat in the other. It rose and ascended until it filled the two horizons, and I turned my eyes. If I wanted to touch the sky, I could. Gabriel turned to me as if he were sitting down, and I recognized the superiority of his knowledge of God over me. A door of the heavens was opened for me, and I saw the greatest light, and beside the veil was the fluttering of pearls and rubies. And what God willed to be revealed was revealed to me.” Then Al-Bazzar said: It is not narrated by anyone except Al-Harith bin Ubaid, and he was a famous man from the people of Basra. I said Al-Harith ibn Ubayd, this is Abu Qudamah Al-Ayadi. Muslim included him in his Sahih, except that Ibn Ma’in weakened him and said: He is nothing. Imam Ahmad said: His hadith is confused. Abu Hatim Al-Razi said: His hadith should be written down but not used as evidence. Ibn Hayyan said: He made many mistakes, so it is not permissible to use it as evidence if he is the only one who narrated it. This hadith is one of the strangest of his narrations, for it contains something strange and odd in its wording and a strange context. Perhaps it is a dream, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in his true form, and he had six hundred wings, each of which filled the horizon, and from his wing fell pearls, rubies, and gems, of which only God knows. Ahmad is the only one who narrated it. Ahmad said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Idris bin Munabbih, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel to see him in his real form. He said: Call upon your Lord. So he called upon his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and a blackness appeared to him from the east, and it began to rise and spread. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw it, he was stunned. So he came to him, revived him, and wiped the spittle from his cheek. Ahmad is the only one to report this. Ibn Asakir narrated it in the biography of Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Uthman ibn Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hubbar ibn al-Aswad, who said: Abu Lahab and his son Utbah had prepared for the Levant, so I prepared with them. His son Utbah said: By God, I will go to Muhammad and seek refuge with him in his Lord, glory be to Him, the Most High. So he set out until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, he disbelieves in the One who drew near, so he came close and was two bow lengths away or nearer. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, unleash upon him one of Your dogs. Then he turned away from him and returned to his father and said: O my son, what did you say to him? So he mentioned to him what he had said, and he said: What did he say to you? He said: He said: O God, unleash one of Your dogs against him. He said: O my son, by God, his prayer is not safe for you. So we went until we reached Al-Sharaat, which was a lion colony. We went down to the monastery of a monk, and the monk said: O Arabs, what brought you to this land? Lions roam freely in it as sheep roam. Abu Lahab said to us: "You know my old age and my rights, and this man has invoked a curse against my son, and by God, I do not trust it against him. Gather your belongings to this monastery and spread out a bed for my son on it, then spread out a bed around it." So we did, and the lion came and smelled our faces. When he did not find what he wanted, he seized it and leaped up and found himself on top of the belongings. He smelled his face, then defeated him and tore his head off. Abu Lahab said: I know that he will not escape the prayer of Muhammad. God the Almighty says: {Then he was two bow lengths away or even nearer} meaning, Gabriel drew near to Muhammad when he descended to him on earth until there was between him and Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) the distance of two bow lengths, i.e., the same as if they were stretched out. This was stated by Mujahid and Qatadah. It was also said that what is meant by this is the distance between the bowstring and its middle. God the Almighty says: {or even nearer}, as we have already mentioned, that this form is used in language to confirm what is being reported and to negate what is greater than it, as in His statement: {Then your hearts hardened after that, so they are like stones or even harder} meaning, they are not softer than stones, rather they are like them or even harder and harder. Similarly, His statement: {They fear men as they fear God or even more}, and His statement: {And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more} meaning, they are not less than them, rather they are truly a hundred thousand or more. This is a confirmation of what was reported, without doubt or hesitation, as this is impossible. And so it is here, this verse, So he was two bow lengths away or even nearer. And what we said, that this approaching, close one who came between him and Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was none other than Gabriel, peace be upon him, and it is the saying of the Mother of the Believers, Aisha, Ibn Masoud, Abu Dharr, and Abu Hurairah, as we will cite their hadiths soon, God willing. Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Muhammad saw his Lord twice in his heart, and he made this one of them. And it came in the hadith of Sharik bin Abi Namir on the authority of Anas in the hadith of the Isra’: Then the Compeller, the Lord of Majesty, drew near and descended. For this reason, many people have spoken about the text of this narration and mentioned strange things in it. If it is authentic, then it is attributed to another time and another story, not that it is an explanation of this verse, for this was while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on earth, not on the night of the Isra’. For this reason he said after it: And indeed, he saw him another time * At the Lote Tree of the Limit. So this is the night of the Isra’, and the first was on earth. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Al-Shawarib told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us, Zur bin Hubaish told us: Abdullah bin Masoud said regarding this verse, Then he was two bow lengths away or nearer, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw Gabriel with six hundred wings. Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The first thing that happened to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was that he saw Gabriel in his sleep in Ajyad. Then he went out to relieve himself, and Gabriel cried out to him: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! So the Messenger of God looked right and left, but did not see anyone, for three days. Then he raised his eyes and saw that he was the second of his two feet, one with the other, on the horizon of the sky, and he said: O Muhammad, Gabriel is calming him. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fled until he entered among the people, and he looked but did not see anything. Then he went out from the people and looked and saw him. Then he entered among the people and did not see anything. Then he went out and looked and saw him. This is the saying of God, the Almighty: "And by the star when it goes down. * Your companion has neither strayed nor erred. * Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination. * It is not but a revelation revealed. * One strong in strength taught him. * Possessor of wisdom. So he rose * And he was on the highest horizon. * Then he drew near and descended" meaning Gabriel to Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon them both. And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. They say: A bow length is half a finger. Some of them said: Two cubits were between them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb with it. And in the hadith of Az-Zuhri from Abu Salamah from Jabir, there is evidence for this. Al-Bukhari narrated from Talq ibn Ghannam from Zaidah from Ash-Shaibani, who said: I asked Zura about the statement: "And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. * Then He revealed to His Servant what He revealed." He said: Abdullah told us that Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw Gabriel and he had six hundred wings. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Buzay` al-Baghdadi told me, Ishaq ibn Mansur told us, Isra`il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah, The heart did not lie about what it saw, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel wearing a fluttering garment that filled the space between the heavens and the earth. Based on what we have mentioned, his statement, Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed, means: So Gabriel revealed to the servant of God, Muhammad, what He revealed, or: So God revealed to His servant Muhammad what He revealed through Gabriel. Both meanings are correct. It was reported on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement, Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed, that he said: God revealed to him, Did He not find you an orphan? “And We have raised high your fame.” Another one said: God revealed to him that Paradise is forbidden to the prophets until you enter it, and to the nations until your nation enters it. God the Almighty said: “The heart did not deny what it saw. Then do you dispute with Him about what he sees?” Muslim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Wakee’ narrated to us, Al-A’mash narrated to us, from Ziyad bin Husayn, from Abu Al-Aaliyah, from Ibn Abbas: The heart did not deny what it saw. “And he had certainly seen Him on another occasion.” He said: He saw Him with his heart twice. Samak narrated it in the same way on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Abu Salih, Al-Suddi and others said: He saw Him with his heart twice. Ibn Mas’ud and others disagreed with him. In a narration on his authority, he stated that he saw Him in general terms, but it is interpreted as being restricted to the heart. Whoever narrated it on the basis of sight has made a strange statement, because nothing authenticated about that from the Companions may God be pleased with them. Al-Baghawi said in his commentary: A group said that he saw Him with his eye, and this is the opinion of Anas, Al-Hasan and Ikrimah, but there is some doubt about it, and God knows best. Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn al-Munhal ibn Safwan told us, Yahya ibn Kathir al-Anbari told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Ja`far, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Muhammad saw his Lord. I said: Didn’t God say: No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. He said: Woe to you, that is when He manifests Himself with His light, which is His light, and he saw his Lord twice. Then he said: Good and strange. He also said: Ibn Abi Omar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Ibn Abbas met Ka’b at Arafat and asked him about something, so he glorified God until the mountains responded to him. Ibn Abbas said: We are the sons of Hashim. Ka’b said: God divided His vision and speech between Muhammad and Moses. He spoke to Moses twice and Muhammad saw Him twice. Masruq said: I entered upon Aisha and said: Did Muhammad see his Lord? She said: You have said something that made my hair stand on end. I said: Wait a minute. Then I recited: He has certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord. She said: Where is he taking you? It is Gabriel. Whoever told you that Muhammad saw his Lord or concealed something that he was commanded to do or knew the five about which God the Most High said: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain. He has greatly slandered God. But he did see Gabriel. He only saw him in his true form twice: once at the Lote Tree of the Limit, and once in Ajyad, and he had six hundred wings that filled the horizon. Al-Nasa’i said: Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Muadh bin Hisham told us, my father told me, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Are you surprised that friendship was for Abraham, speech was for Moses, and vision was for Muhammad, peace be upon them? In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him and his family: Have you seen your Lord? He said: Light, how can I see Him? In another narration: I saw a light. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa’id al-Ashj told us, on the authority of Abu Khalid, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, who said: They said: O Messenger of God, have you seen your Lord? He said: I saw Him with my heart twice. Then he recited: The heart did not lie about what it saw. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Hamid, on the authority of Mihran, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: We said: O Messenger of God, have you seen your Lord? He said: I did not see Him with my eyes, but I saw Him with my heart twice. Then he recited: Then He drew near and came closer. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Ansari told us, Ibad bin Mansour told me: I asked Ikrimah about His statement: The heart did not lie about what it saw. Ikrimah said: Do you want me to tell you that it saw Him? I said: Yes. He said: He saw Him, then he saw Him. He said: So I asked Al-Hasan about it, and he said: He saw His glory, His greatness, and His cloak. My father told us, Muhammad bin Mujahid told us, Abu Amir Al-Aqdi told us, Abu Khaldah told us on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Have you seen your Lord? He said: I saw a river and I saw behind the river a veil, and I saw behind the veil a light other than which I had never seen. This is very strange. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Aswad ibn Amir told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, then it is a hadith whose chain of transmission meets the criteria of authenticity, but it is an abbreviated version of the hadith of a dream, as Imam Ahmad also narrated: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord came to me last night in the most beautiful form - I think he meant in a dream - and said: O Muhammad, do you know what the highest assembly disputes about? I said: No. Then He placed His hand between my shoulders until I felt its coolness between my breasts - or he said my throat - and I knew what was in the heavens and what was on the earth. Then He said: O Muhammad, do you know what the highest assembly disputes about? I said: Yes, they dispute about…” Expiations and degrees. He said: What are the expiations? He said: I said: Staying in the mosques after the prayers, walking to the congregational prayers, and performing ablution thoroughly even in difficult situations. Whoever does that will live well and die well, and he will be free from his sins as on the day his mother bore him. And he said: Say, O Muhammad, when you pray: O God, I ask You to do good deeds, abandon evil deeds, and love the poor. And if You intend a trial for Your servants, take me to You without being tested. He said: And the degrees are giving food, spreading peace, and praying at night while people are asleep. Something similar was mentioned at the end of Surah Sad from Muadh. Ibn Jarir narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it contains another context and a strange addition. He said: Ahmad ibn Isa al-Tamimi told me, Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Sayyar told me, my father told me on the authority of Sa`id ibn Zurbi on the authority of Umar ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ata` on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw my Lord in the most beautiful form, and He said to me: ‘O Muhammad, do you know what the highest assembly disputes about?’ I said: ‘No, O Lord.’ So He placed His hand between my shoulders, and I felt its coolness between my breasts, and I knew what was in the heavens and the earth, and I said: ‘O Lord, regarding the degrees and expiations, and moving the feet to the congregations, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer.’ I said: ‘O Lord, You took Abraham as a friend and spoke to Moses directly, and You did this and that.’ He said: ‘Did I not expand your breast for you? Did I not remove your burden from you? Did I not do to you? Did I not do to you?’ He said: ‘Then He confided in me things that I was not permitted to relate to you.’ He said: ‘This is what He said in His Book: “Then He approached and came closer, and was two bow lengths or nearer, and revealed to His Servant what He revealed.’ What…” The heart lied about what it saw. So He placed the light of my sight in my heart, so I looked at Him with my heart. Its chain of transmission is weak. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned with his chain of transmission back to Hubbar ibn al-Aswad may God be pleased with him that when Utbah ibn Abi Lahab went out to trade with the people of Ash-Sham, he said to the people of Makkah, Know that I am an unbeliever in the One who drew near and hung down. When his words reached the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), he said, God has set upon him one of His dogs. Hubbar said, “So I was with them and we camped in a land with many lions. I saw a lion come and sniff the heads of the people one by one until it stepped over to Utbah and cut off his head from among them.” Ibn Ishaq and others mentioned in the Seerah that this happened in the land of Az-Zarqa’, and it was said in As-Sarat, and that he went against them that night, and that they made him stay among them and slept around him, then the lion came and began to roar, then stepped over to them and crushed his head. May God curse it. And the Almighty said: And he had already seen him in another descent * At the Lote Tree of the Limit * Near it is the Garden of Refuge. This is the second time that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in the form in which God created him, and it was on the Night of the Isra’. We have already presented the hadiths related about the Isra’ with their chains of transmission and wordings at the beginning of Surat Subhan, so there is no need to repeat them here. It was mentioned that Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, used to confirm the vision on the night of the Isra’ and he used this verse as evidence, and a group of the early and later generations followed him. However, groups of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, the Followers, and others disagreed with him. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Bahdalah, Anzar ibn Hubaish, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, regarding this verse, And he had seen him on another occasion, * at the Lote Tree of the Limit, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I saw Gabriel, and he had six hundred wings, from which were scattered feathers of pearls and rubies. This is a good, strong chain of transmission. Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Adam told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Jami’ ibn Abi Rashid, on the authority of Abi Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in his true form, and he had six hundred wings, each of which filled the horizon, and from his wing fell…” The exaggerations of the pearls and rubies, God knows best. Its chain of transmission is also good. Imam Ahmad also said: Zaid ibn al-Hubab told us, Husayn told us, Asim ibn Bahdalah told us, he said, I heard Shaqiq ibn Salamah say: I heard Ibn Masoud say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: I saw Gabriel on the Lote Tree of the Limit and he had six hundred wings. I asked Asim about wings and he refused to tell me. He said, So some of his companions told me that a wing is the distance between the east and the west. This is also a good chain of transmission. Ahmad said: Zaid ibn al-Hubab told us, Husayn told us, Asim ibn Bahdalah told us, Shaqiq ibn Salamah told me: I heard Ibn Masoud say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me in a green garment with pearls hanging from it.” Its chain of transmission is also good. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Ismail, Aamir told us: Masruq came to Aisha and said: O Mother of the Believers, did Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) see his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic? She said: Glory be to God, my hair stood on end when you said this. Where are you from three things, whoever told you about them has lied: Whoever told you that Muhammad saw his Lord has lied. Then you read: No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. “It is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil.” Whoever told you that He knows what will happen tomorrow has lied. Then you read: “Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs.” Whoever told you that Muhammad concealed things has lied. Then you read: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. But he saw Gabriel in his true form twice. Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad bin Abi Uday narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I was with Aisha and I said: Doesn’t God say: And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon and And he certainly saw him on another occasion. She said: I am the first of this nation to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: That was Gabriel. He did not see him in the form in which he was created except twice. He saw him descending from the heaven to the earth, his great creation filling the space between the heaven and the earth. They included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Al-Sha’bi with it. Narrated by Abu Dharr Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammam told us, Qatadah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, who said: I said to Abu Dharr, “If you had seen the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), I would have asked him.” He said, And what would you have asked him? He said, I would have asked him, ‘Did he see his Lord?’ He said, I did ask him, ‘I saw Him as light, how could I see Him?’ This is how it appears in the narration of Imam Ahmad. Muslim narrated it through two chains of transmission with two wordings. He said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), Did you see your Lord? He said, Light, how could I see Him. And he said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Muadh bin Hisham told us, my father told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, who said: I said to Abu Dharr, “If you had seen the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), I would have asked him.” He said, What would you ask him about? He said, I would have asked him, ‘Did you see your Lord?’ Abu Dharr said: I asked him and he said, I saw a light. Al-Khalal mentioned in his book, Ilal, that Imam Ahmad was asked about this hadith and he said, I have always disapproved of it and I do not know what its reason is. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Amr ibn Awn al-Wasiti told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: He saw Him with his heart, but did not see Him with his eyes. Ibn Khuzaymah tried to claim that there was an interruption in the chain of transmission between Abdullah ibn Shaqiq and Abu Dharr. As for Ibn al-Jawzi, he interpreted it as meaning that Abu Dharr might have asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before the Isra’ and he answered him as he did. If he had asked him after the Isra’, he would have answered him positively. This is very weak, because Aisha, the Mother of the Believers may God be pleased with her, asked about that after the Isra’ and it was not proven that she had seen Him. Whoever says that he addressed her according to her level of intellect or tried to prove her wrong in what she believed, like Ibn Khuzaymah in the Book of Tawhid, then he is the one who is mistaken, and God knows best. An-Nasa’i said: Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Yazid ibn Sharik, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw his Lord with his heart, but did not see Him with his sight. It was proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Ali bin Masahr, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that he said regarding the Almighty’s statement: And he had certainly seen him on another occasion, he said that he saw Gabriel, peace be upon him. Mujahid said about the statement of God, And he had already seen him on another occasion, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in his original form twice. Qatadah, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas and others said the same. And the statement of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, When that which covers the lote-tree covers has already been mentioned in the hadiths of the Night Journey that it was covered by angels like crows, and the light of the Lord covered it, and colors covered it, I do not know what they are. And Imam Ahmad said: Malik ibn Mughul told us, Az-Zubayr ibn Adi told us, on the authority of Talhah, on the authority of Marrah, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree of the Limit, which is in the seventh heaven. Whatever ascends from the earth ends there, and whatever descends from above it ends there, and whatever descends from above it ends there, and he is taken there. When that which covers the lote-tree covers he said: A bed of gold. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given three things: He was given the five daily prayers, he was given the last verses of Surat Al-Baqarah, and forgiveness was given to those of his nation who do not associate anything with God for the sins committed. It was narrated exclusively by Muslim. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said, on the authority of al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah or someone else - Abu Ja`far was unsure - who said: When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was taken on the Night Journey al-Isra, he reached the lote-tree. It was said to him: This is the lote-tree, and the light of the Creator covered it, and the angels covered it like crows when they perch on a tree. Then he spoke to him and said: Ask. Ibn Abi Nujayh said, on the authority of Mujahid: When that which covers the lote-tree covers it He said: The branches of the lote-tree were pearls, rubies and emeralds. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) saw them and saw his Lord with his heart. Ibn Zayd said: It was said: O Messenger of God, what did you see covering that lote-tree? He said: I saw a moth of gold covering it, and I saw on each of its leaves an angel standing, glorifying God, the Almighty and Majestic. And the Almighty’s saying: His sight did not swerve, nor did he transgress. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He did not go right or left. And he did not transgress: He did not go beyond what he was commanded to do. This is a great characteristic of steadfastness and obedience, for he did nothing but what he was commanded to do, and he did not ask for more than what he was given. How beautiful is what the poet said: He saw the paradise of refuge and what is above it, and if anyone else had seen what he had seen, he would have been lost. And the Almighty’s saying: He has certainly seen some of the greatest signs of his Lord is like His saying: That We may show you some of Our greatest signs, meaning those that indicate Our power and greatness. And with these two verses, those of the Sunnis who believed that the vision that night did not occur were proven by saying: He has certainly seen some of the greatest signs of his Lord. And if he had seen his Lord, he would have informed about that and told that to the people. And the explanation of that has been presented in Surat Subhan. Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr told us, Muhammad ibn Talhah told us, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Qays, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Abi al-Kahtalah. Muhammad said, I think it was on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, that he said: Muhammad did not see Gabriel in his true form except twice: Once, he asked him to show him himself in his true form, so he showed him his form and the horizon was blocked. The other time, he ascended with him when he ascended with him. And His statement: “And he was at the highest horizon. Then he drew near and came closer. And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. And He revealed to His Servant what He revealed.” When Gabriel perceived his Lord, the Almighty, he returned to his true form and prostrated. So His statement: “And he had certainly seen him in another descent. At the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary. Near it is the Garden of Refuge. When that which covered the Lote Tree covered him. His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress. He had certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord.” He said: The creation of Gabriel, peace be upon him. Ahmad narrated it in this way, but it is strange.
53:6: God the Almighty says, informing about His servant and Messenger Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that the knowledge he brought to the people was strong in strength, that is, Gabriel, peace be upon him, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, it is the word of an honored Messenger, * Possessor of strength with the Lord of the Throne, firmly established, * Obeyed and trustworthy. And He said here, of great stature, meaning of great strength, as stated by Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Abbas said: of good looks. Qatadah said: of tall, handsome character. There is no contradiction between the two statements, as he, peace be upon him, was of good looks and great strength. It was reported in the authentic hadith narrated by Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Charity is not permissible for a rich person or one of good looks. And God the Almighty’s statement: then he rose up means Gabriel, peace be upon him, as stated by Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas. And he was at the highest horizon, that is, Gabriel rose up at the highest horizon, as stated by Ikrimah and others. Ikrimah said: and the highest horizon is from which dawn comes. Mujahid said: it is the place where the sun rises. Qatada said: It is the one from which the day comes, and Ibn Zayd and others said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Masraf bin Amr al-Yami Abu al-Qasim told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Muhammad bin Talha bin Masraf told us, my father told me, on the authority of al-Walid - he is Ibn Qais - on the authority of Ishaq bin Abi al-Kahtalah - I think he mentioned it on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud - that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not see Gabriel in his true form except twice: As for the first time, he asked him to see him in his true form, so the horizon was blocked. And as for the second, he was with him where he ascended, so that is his saying: And he is on the highest horizon. Ibn Jarir said here a saying that I have not seen from anyone else, nor did he narrate it from anyone. The gist of it is that he went to the meaning that he and Muhammad, may God bless him and grant him peace, were leveled, that is, they were both leveled on the highest horizon, and that was on the night of the Isra’. This is what he said, and no one agreed with him on that. Then he began to explain what he said from the Arabic perspective, so he said: It is like his saying: When we and our fathers were dust, so he connected with fathers to the one referred to in we without making we clear. So is his saying that he was leveled and he. Al-Farra’ mentioned on the authority of some Arabs that he recited to him: Have you not seen that the spring hardens and becomes uneven? And the castor oil that is split This is what he said from the Arabic perspective, but the meaning does not support it, because this vision of Gabriel did not take place on the night of the Isra’, but rather before it, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on earth, so Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended to him and approached him while he was in the form in which God created him, with six hundred wings. Then he saw him after that another descent at the Lote Tree of the Limit, meaning the night of the Isra’. This first vision was in the beginning of the mission after Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him the first time, and God revealed to him the beginning of Surat Al-Iqra’. Then the revelation stopped for a period during which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went repeatedly to throw himself down from the tops of mountains. Whenever he was about to do that, Gabriel called out to him from the air, O Muhammad, you are truly the Messenger of God and I am Gabriel. This calmed him down and made him happy. Whenever the matter took longer, he returned to the same state until Gabriel and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared to him in Al-Abtah in the form in which God created him, with six hundred wings and the greatness of his creation filling the horizon. He approached him and revealed to him from God Almighty what He had commanded him to do. At that point, he knew the greatness of the angel who had come to him with the message and the majesty of his status and the loftiness of his position with his Creator who had sent him to him. As for the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar in his Musnad, where he said: Salamah bin Shabib narrated to us, Saeed bin Mansour narrated to us, Al-Harith bin Ubaid narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Joni, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “While I was sitting, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came and poked me between my shoulders. I went to a tree in which were the nests of birds. He sat in one of them, and I sat in the other. It rose and ascended until it filled the two horizons, and I turned my eyes. If I wanted to touch the sky, I could. Gabriel turned to me as if he were sitting down, and I recognized the superiority of his knowledge of God over me. A door of the heavens was opened for me, and I saw the greatest light, and beside the veil was the fluttering of pearls and rubies. And what God willed to be revealed was revealed to me.” Then Al-Bazzar said: It is not narrated by anyone except Al-Harith bin Ubaid, and he was a famous man from the people of Basra. I said Al-Harith ibn Ubayd, this is Abu Qudamah Al-Ayadi. Muslim included him in his Sahih, except that Ibn Ma’in weakened him and said: He is nothing. Imam Ahmad said: His hadith is confused. Abu Hatim Al-Razi said: His hadith should be written down but not used as evidence. Ibn Hayyan said: He made many mistakes, so it is not permissible to use it as evidence if he is the only one who narrated it. This hadith is one of the strangest of his narrations, for it contains something strange and odd in its wording and a strange context. Perhaps it is a dream, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in his true form, and he had six hundred wings, each of which filled the horizon, and from his wing fell pearls, rubies, and gems, of which only God knows. Ahmad is the only one who narrated it. Ahmad said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Idris bin Munabbih, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel to see him in his real form. He said: Call upon your Lord. So he called upon his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and a blackness appeared to him from the east, and it began to rise and spread. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw it, he was stunned. So he came to him, revived him, and wiped the spittle from his cheek. Ahmad is the only one to report this. Ibn Asakir narrated it in the biography of Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Uthman ibn Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hubbar ibn al-Aswad, who said: Abu Lahab and his son Utbah had prepared for the Levant, so I prepared with them. His son Utbah said: By God, I will go to Muhammad and seek refuge with him in his Lord, glory be to Him, the Most High. So he set out until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, he disbelieves in the One who drew near, so he came close and was two bow lengths away or nearer. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, unleash upon him one of Your dogs. Then he turned away from him and returned to his father and said: O my son, what did you say to him? So he mentioned to him what he had said, and he said: What did he say to you? He said: He said: O God, unleash one of Your dogs against him. He said: O my son, by God, his prayer is not safe for you. So we went until we reached Al-Sharaat, which was a lion colony. We went down to the monastery of a monk, and the monk said: O Arabs, what brought you to this land? Lions roam freely in it as sheep roam. Abu Lahab said to us: "You know my old age and my rights, and this man has invoked a curse against my son, and by God, I do not trust it against him. Gather your belongings to this monastery and spread out a bed for my son on it, then spread out a bed around it." So we did, and the lion came and smelled our faces. When he did not find what he wanted, he seized it and leaped up and found himself on top of the belongings. He smelled his face, then defeated him and tore his head off. Abu Lahab said: I know that he will not escape the prayer of Muhammad. God the Almighty says: {Then he was two bow lengths away or even nearer} meaning, Gabriel drew near to Muhammad when he descended to him on earth until there was between him and Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) the distance of two bow lengths, i.e., the same as if they were stretched out. This was stated by Mujahid and Qatadah. It was also said that what is meant by this is the distance between the bowstring and its middle. God the Almighty says: {or even nearer}, as we have already mentioned, that this form is used in language to confirm what is being reported and to negate what is greater than it, as in His statement: {Then your hearts hardened after that, so they are like stones or even harder} meaning, they are not softer than stones, rather they are like them or even harder and harder. Similarly, His statement: {They fear men as they fear God or even more}, and His statement: {And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more} meaning, they are not less than them, rather they are truly a hundred thousand or more. This is a confirmation of what was reported, without doubt or hesitation, as this is impossible. And so it is here, this verse, So he was two bow lengths away or even nearer. And what we said, that this approaching, close one who came between him and Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was none other than Gabriel, peace be upon him, and it is the saying of the Mother of the Believers, Aisha, Ibn Masoud, Abu Dharr, and Abu Hurairah, as we will cite their hadiths soon, God willing. Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Muhammad saw his Lord twice in his heart, and he made this one of them. And it came in the hadith of Sharik bin Abi Namir on the authority of Anas in the hadith of the Isra’: Then the Compeller, the Lord of Majesty, drew near and descended. For this reason, many people have spoken about the text of this narration and mentioned strange things in it. If it is authentic, then it is attributed to another time and another story, not that it is an explanation of this verse, for this was while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on earth, not on the night of the Isra’. For this reason he said after it: And indeed, he saw him another time * At the Lote Tree of the Limit. So this is the night of the Isra’, and the first was on earth. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Al-Shawarib told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us, Zur bin Hubaish told us: Abdullah bin Masoud said regarding this verse, Then he was two bow lengths away or nearer, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw Gabriel with six hundred wings. Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The first thing that happened to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was that he saw Gabriel in his sleep in Ajyad. Then he went out to relieve himself, and Gabriel cried out to him: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! So the Messenger of God looked right and left, but did not see anyone, for three days. Then he raised his eyes and saw that he was the second of his two feet, one with the other, on the horizon of the sky, and he said: O Muhammad, Gabriel is calming him. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fled until he entered among the people, and he looked but did not see anything. Then he went out from the people and looked and saw him. Then he entered among the people and did not see anything. Then he went out and looked and saw him. This is the saying of God, the Almighty: "And by the star when it goes down. * Your companion has neither strayed nor erred. * Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination. * It is not but a revelation revealed. * One strong in strength taught him. * Possessor of wisdom. So he rose * And he was on the highest horizon. * Then he drew near and descended" meaning Gabriel to Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon them both. And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. They say: A bow length is half a finger. Some of them said: Two cubits were between them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb with it. And in the hadith of Az-Zuhri from Abu Salamah from Jabir, there is evidence for this. Al-Bukhari narrated from Talq ibn Ghannam from Zaidah from Ash-Shaibani, who said: I asked Zura about the statement: "And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. * Then He revealed to His Servant what He revealed." He said: Abdullah told us that Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw Gabriel and he had six hundred wings. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Buzay` al-Baghdadi told me, Ishaq ibn Mansur told us, Isra`il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah, The heart did not lie about what it saw, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel wearing a fluttering garment that filled the space between the heavens and the earth. Based on what we have mentioned, his statement, Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed, means: So Gabriel revealed to the servant of God, Muhammad, what He revealed, or: So God revealed to His servant Muhammad what He revealed through Gabriel. Both meanings are correct. It was reported on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement, Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed, that he said: God revealed to him, Did He not find you an orphan? “And We have raised high your fame.” Another one said: God revealed to him that Paradise is forbidden to the prophets until you enter it, and to the nations until your nation enters it. God the Almighty said: “The heart did not deny what it saw. Then do you dispute with Him about what he sees?” Muslim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Wakee’ narrated to us, Al-A’mash narrated to us, from Ziyad bin Husayn, from Abu Al-Aaliyah, from Ibn Abbas: The heart did not deny what it saw. “And he had certainly seen Him on another occasion.” He said: He saw Him with his heart twice. Samak narrated it in the same way on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Abu Salih, Al-Suddi and others said: He saw Him with his heart twice. Ibn Mas’ud and others disagreed with him. In a narration on his authority, he stated that he saw Him in general terms, but it is interpreted as being restricted to the heart. Whoever narrated it on the basis of sight has made a strange statement, because nothing authenticated about that from the Companions may God be pleased with them. Al-Baghawi said in his commentary: A group said that he saw Him with his eye, and this is the opinion of Anas, Al-Hasan and Ikrimah, but there is some doubt about it, and God knows best. Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn al-Munhal ibn Safwan told us, Yahya ibn Kathir al-Anbari told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Ja`far, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Muhammad saw his Lord. I said: Didn’t God say: No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. He said: Woe to you, that is when He manifests Himself with His light, which is His light, and he saw his Lord twice. Then he said: Good and strange. He also said: Ibn Abi Omar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Ibn Abbas met Ka’b at Arafat and asked him about something, so he glorified God until the mountains responded to him. Ibn Abbas said: We are the sons of Hashim. Ka’b said: God divided His vision and speech between Muhammad and Moses. He spoke to Moses twice and Muhammad saw Him twice. Masruq said: I entered upon Aisha and said: Did Muhammad see his Lord? She said: You have said something that made my hair stand on end. I said: Wait a minute. Then I recited: He has certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord. She said: Where is he taking you? It is Gabriel. Whoever told you that Muhammad saw his Lord or concealed something that he was commanded to do or knew the five about which God the Most High said: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain. He has greatly slandered God. But he did see Gabriel. He only saw him in his true form twice: once at the Lote Tree of the Limit, and once in Ajyad, and he had six hundred wings that filled the horizon. Al-Nasa’i said: Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Muadh bin Hisham told us, my father told me, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Are you surprised that friendship was for Abraham, speech was for Moses, and vision was for Muhammad, peace be upon them? In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him and his family: Have you seen your Lord? He said: Light, how can I see Him? In another narration: I saw a light. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa’id al-Ashj told us, on the authority of Abu Khalid, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, who said: They said: O Messenger of God, have you seen your Lord? He said: I saw Him with my heart twice. Then he recited: The heart did not lie about what it saw. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Hamid, on the authority of Mihran, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: We said: O Messenger of God, have you seen your Lord? He said: I did not see Him with my eyes, but I saw Him with my heart twice. Then he recited: Then He drew near and came closer. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Ansari told us, Ibad bin Mansour told me: I asked Ikrimah about His statement: The heart did not lie about what it saw. Ikrimah said: Do you want me to tell you that it saw Him? I said: Yes. He said: He saw Him, then he saw Him. He said: So I asked Al-Hasan about it, and he said: He saw His glory, His greatness, and His cloak. My father told us, Muhammad bin Mujahid told us, Abu Amir Al-Aqdi told us, Abu Khaldah told us on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Have you seen your Lord? He said: I saw a river and I saw behind the river a veil, and I saw behind the veil a light other than which I had never seen. This is very strange. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Aswad ibn Amir told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, then it is a hadith whose chain of transmission meets the criteria of authenticity, but it is an abbreviated version of the hadith of a dream, as Imam Ahmad also narrated: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord came to me last night in the most beautiful form - I think he meant in a dream - and said: O Muhammad, do you know what the highest assembly disputes about? I said: No. Then He placed His hand between my shoulders until I felt its coolness between my breasts - or he said my throat - and I knew what was in the heavens and what was on the earth. Then He said: O Muhammad, do you know what the highest assembly disputes about? I said: Yes, they dispute about…” Expiations and degrees. He said: What are the expiations? He said: I said: Staying in the mosques after the prayers, walking to the congregational prayers, and performing ablution thoroughly even in difficult situations. Whoever does that will live well and die well, and he will be free from his sins as on the day his mother bore him. And he said: Say, O Muhammad, when you pray: O God, I ask You to do good deeds, abandon evil deeds, and love the poor. And if You intend a trial for Your servants, take me to You without being tested. He said: And the degrees are giving food, spreading peace, and praying at night while people are asleep. Something similar was mentioned at the end of Surah Sad from Muadh. Ibn Jarir narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it contains another context and a strange addition. He said: Ahmad ibn Isa al-Tamimi told me, Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Sayyar told me, my father told me on the authority of Sa`id ibn Zurbi on the authority of Umar ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ata` on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw my Lord in the most beautiful form, and He said to me: ‘O Muhammad, do you know what the highest assembly disputes about?’ I said: ‘No, O Lord.’ So He placed His hand between my shoulders, and I felt its coolness between my breasts, and I knew what was in the heavens and the earth, and I said: ‘O Lord, regarding the degrees and expiations, and moving the feet to the congregations, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer.’ I said: ‘O Lord, You took Abraham as a friend and spoke to Moses directly, and You did this and that.’ He said: ‘Did I not expand your breast for you? Did I not remove your burden from you? Did I not do to you? Did I not do to you?’ He said: ‘Then He confided in me things that I was not permitted to relate to you.’ He said: ‘This is what He said in His Book: “Then He approached and came closer, and was two bow lengths or nearer, and revealed to His Servant what He revealed.’ What…” The heart lied about what it saw. So He placed the light of my sight in my heart, so I looked at Him with my heart. Its chain of transmission is weak. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned with his chain of transmission back to Hubbar ibn al-Aswad may God be pleased with him that when Utbah ibn Abi Lahab went out to trade with the people of Ash-Sham, he said to the people of Makkah, Know that I am an unbeliever in the One who drew near and hung down. When his words reached the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), he said, God has set upon him one of His dogs. Hubbar said, “So I was with them and we camped in a land with many lions. I saw a lion come and sniff the heads of the people one by one until it stepped over to Utbah and cut off his head from among them.” Ibn Ishaq and others mentioned in the Seerah that this happened in the land of Az-Zarqa’, and it was said in As-Sarat, and that he went against them that night, and that they made him stay among them and slept around him, then the lion came and began to roar, then stepped over to them and crushed his head. May God curse it. And the Almighty said: And he had already seen him in another descent * At the Lote Tree of the Limit * Near it is the Garden of Refuge. This is the second time that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in the form in which God created him, and it was on the Night of the Isra’. We have already presented the hadiths related about the Isra’ with their chains of transmission and wordings at the beginning of Surat Subhan, so there is no need to repeat them here. It was mentioned that Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, used to confirm the vision on the night of the Isra’ and he used this verse as evidence, and a group of the early and later generations followed him. However, groups of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, the Followers, and others disagreed with him. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Bahdalah, Anzar ibn Hubaish, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, regarding this verse, And he had seen him on another occasion, * at the Lote Tree of the Limit, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I saw Gabriel, and he had six hundred wings, from which were scattered feathers of pearls and rubies. This is a good, strong chain of transmission. Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Adam told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Jami’ ibn Abi Rashid, on the authority of Abi Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in his true form, and he had six hundred wings, each of which filled the horizon, and from his wing fell…” The exaggerations of the pearls and rubies, God knows best. Its chain of transmission is also good. Imam Ahmad also said: Zaid ibn al-Hubab told us, Husayn told us, Asim ibn Bahdalah told us, he said, I heard Shaqiq ibn Salamah say: I heard Ibn Masoud say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: I saw Gabriel on the Lote Tree of the Limit and he had six hundred wings. I asked Asim about wings and he refused to tell me. He said, So some of his companions told me that a wing is the distance between the east and the west. This is also a good chain of transmission. Ahmad said: Zaid ibn al-Hubab told us, Husayn told us, Asim ibn Bahdalah told us, Shaqiq ibn Salamah told me: I heard Ibn Masoud say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me in a green garment with pearls hanging from it.” Its chain of transmission is also good. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Ismail, Aamir told us: Masruq came to Aisha and said: O Mother of the Believers, did Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) see his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic? She said: Glory be to God, my hair stood on end when you said this. Where are you from three things, whoever told you about them has lied: Whoever told you that Muhammad saw his Lord has lied. Then you read: No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. “It is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil.” Whoever told you that He knows what will happen tomorrow has lied. Then you read: “Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs.” Whoever told you that Muhammad concealed things has lied. Then you read: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. But he saw Gabriel in his true form twice. Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad bin Abi Uday narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I was with Aisha and I said: Doesn’t God say: And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon and And he certainly saw him on another occasion. She said: I am the first of this nation to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: That was Gabriel. He did not see him in the form in which he was created except twice. He saw him descending from the heaven to the earth, his great creation filling the space between the heaven and the earth. They included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Al-Sha’bi with it. Narrated by Abu Dharr Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammam told us, Qatadah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, who said: I said to Abu Dharr, “If you had seen the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), I would have asked him.” He said, And what would you have asked him? He said, I would have asked him, ‘Did he see his Lord?’ He said, I did ask him, ‘I saw Him as light, how could I see Him?’ This is how it appears in the narration of Imam Ahmad. Muslim narrated it through two chains of transmission with two wordings. He said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), Did you see your Lord? He said, Light, how could I see Him. And he said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Muadh bin Hisham told us, my father told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, who said: I said to Abu Dharr, “If you had seen the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), I would have asked him.” He said, What would you ask him about? He said, I would have asked him, ‘Did you see your Lord?’ Abu Dharr said: I asked him and he said, I saw a light. Al-Khalal mentioned in his book, Ilal, that Imam Ahmad was asked about this hadith and he said, I have always disapproved of it and I do not know what its reason is. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Amr ibn Awn al-Wasiti told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: He saw Him with his heart, but did not see Him with his eyes. Ibn Khuzaymah tried to claim that there was an interruption in the chain of transmission between Abdullah ibn Shaqiq and Abu Dharr. As for Ibn al-Jawzi, he interpreted it as meaning that Abu Dharr might have asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before the Isra’ and he answered him as he did. If he had asked him after the Isra’, he would have answered him positively. This is very weak, because Aisha, the Mother of the Believers may God be pleased with her, asked about that after the Isra’ and it was not proven that she had seen Him. Whoever says that he addressed her according to her level of intellect or tried to prove her wrong in what she believed, like Ibn Khuzaymah in the Book of Tawhid, then he is the one who is mistaken, and God knows best. An-Nasa’i said: Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Yazid ibn Sharik, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw his Lord with his heart, but did not see Him with his sight. It was proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Ali bin Masahr, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that he said regarding the Almighty’s statement: And he had certainly seen him on another occasion, he said that he saw Gabriel, peace be upon him. Mujahid said about the statement of God, And he had already seen him on another occasion, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in his original form twice. Qatadah, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas and others said the same. And the statement of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, When that which covers the lote-tree covers has already been mentioned in the hadiths of the Night Journey that it was covered by angels like crows, and the light of the Lord covered it, and colors covered it, I do not know what they are. And Imam Ahmad said: Malik ibn Mughul told us, Az-Zubayr ibn Adi told us, on the authority of Talhah, on the authority of Marrah, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree of the Limit, which is in the seventh heaven. Whatever ascends from the earth ends there, and whatever descends from above it ends there, and whatever descends from above it ends there, and he is taken there. When that which covers the lote-tree covers he said: A bed of gold. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given three things: He was given the five daily prayers, he was given the last verses of Surat Al-Baqarah, and forgiveness was given to those of his nation who do not associate anything with God for the sins committed. It was narrated exclusively by Muslim. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said, on the authority of al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah or someone else - Abu Ja`far was unsure - who said: When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was taken on the Night Journey al-Isra, he reached the lote-tree. It was said to him: This is the lote-tree, and the light of the Creator covered it, and the angels covered it like crows when they perch on a tree. Then he spoke to him and said: Ask. Ibn Abi Nujayh said, on the authority of Mujahid: When that which covers the lote-tree covers it He said: The branches of the lote-tree were pearls, rubies and emeralds. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) saw them and saw his Lord with his heart. Ibn Zayd said: It was said: O Messenger of God, what did you see covering that lote-tree? He said: I saw a moth of gold covering it, and I saw on each of its leaves an angel standing, glorifying God, the Almighty and Majestic. And the Almighty’s saying: His sight did not swerve, nor did he transgress. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He did not go right or left. And he did not transgress: He did not go beyond what he was commanded to do. This is a great characteristic of steadfastness and obedience, for he did nothing but what he was commanded to do, and he did not ask for more than what he was given. How beautiful is what the poet said: He saw the paradise of refuge and what is above it, and if anyone else had seen what he had seen, he would have been lost. And the Almighty’s saying: He has certainly seen some of the greatest signs of his Lord is like His saying: That We may show you some of Our greatest signs, meaning those that indicate Our power and greatness. And with these two verses, those of the Sunnis who believed that the vision that night did not occur were proven by saying: He has certainly seen some of the greatest signs of his Lord. And if he had seen his Lord, he would have informed about that and told that to the people. And the explanation of that has been presented in Surat Subhan. Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr told us, Muhammad ibn Talhah told us, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Qays, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Abi al-Kahtalah. Muhammad said, I think it was on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, that he said: Muhammad did not see Gabriel in his true form except twice: Once, he asked him to show him himself in his true form, so he showed him his form and the horizon was blocked. The other time, he ascended with him when he ascended with him. And His statement: “And he was at the highest horizon. Then he drew near and came closer. And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. And He revealed to His Servant what He revealed.” When Gabriel perceived his Lord, the Almighty, he returned to his true form and prostrated. So His statement: “And he had certainly seen him in another descent. At the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary. Near it is the Garden of Refuge. When that which covered the Lote Tree covered him. His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress. He had certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord.” He said: The creation of Gabriel, peace be upon him. Ahmad narrated it in this way, but it is strange.
53:7: God the Almighty says, informing about His servant and Messenger Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, that the knowledge he brought to the people was strong in strength, that is, Gabriel, peace be upon him, as God the Almighty said: Indeed, it is the word of an honored Messenger, * Possessor of strength with the Lord of the Throne, firmly established, * Obeyed and trustworthy. And He said here, of great stature, meaning of great strength, as stated by Mujahid, Al-Hasan, and Ibn Zayd. Ibn Abbas said: of good looks. Qatadah said: of tall, handsome character. There is no contradiction between the two statements, as he, peace be upon him, was of good looks and great strength. It was reported in the authentic hadith narrated by Ibn Umar and Abu Hurayrah that the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, said: Charity is not permissible for a rich person or one of good looks. And God the Almighty’s statement: then he rose up means Gabriel, peace be upon him, as stated by Al-Hasan, Mujahid, Qatadah, and Al-Rabi’ ibn Anas. And he was at the highest horizon, that is, Gabriel rose up at the highest horizon, as stated by Ikrimah and others. Ikrimah said: and the highest horizon is from which dawn comes. Mujahid said: it is the place where the sun rises. Qatada said: It is the one from which the day comes, and Ibn Zayd and others said the same. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur’ah told us, Masraf bin Amr al-Yami Abu al-Qasim told us, Abd al-Rahman bin Muhammad bin Talha bin Masraf told us, my father told me, on the authority of al-Walid - he is Ibn Qais - on the authority of Ishaq bin Abi al-Kahtalah - I think he mentioned it on the authority of Abdullah bin Mas’ud - that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not see Gabriel in his true form except twice: As for the first time, he asked him to see him in his true form, so the horizon was blocked. And as for the second, he was with him where he ascended, so that is his saying: And he is on the highest horizon. Ibn Jarir said here a saying that I have not seen from anyone else, nor did he narrate it from anyone.
