So is his saying that he was leveled and he. Al-Farra’ mentioned on the authority of some Arabs that he recited to him: Haven't you seen that the spring hardens and becomes uneven? And the castor oil that is split This is what he said from the Arabic perspective, but the meaning does not support it, because this vision of Gabriel did not take place on the night of the Isra’, but rather before it, and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on earth, so Gabriel, peace be upon him, descended to him and approached him while he was in the form in which God created him, with six hundred wings. Then he saw him after that another descent at the Lote Tree of the Limit, meaning the night of the Isra’. This first vision was in the beginning of the mission after Gabriel, peace be upon him, came to him the first time, and God revealed to him the beginning of Surat Al-Iqra’. Then the revelation stopped for a period during which the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, went repeatedly to throw himself down from the tops of mountains. Whenever he was about to do that, Gabriel called out to him from the air, O Muhammad, you are truly the Messenger of God and I am Gabriel. This calmed him down and made him happy. Whenever the matter took longer, he returned to the same state until Gabriel and the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, appeared to him in Al-Abtah in the form in which God created him, with six hundred wings and the greatness of his creation filling the horizon. He approached him and revealed to him from God Almighty what He had commanded him to do. At that point, he knew the greatness of the angel who had come to him with the message and the majesty of his status and the loftiness of his position with his Creator who had sent him to him. As for the hadith narrated by Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Al-Bazzar in his Musnad, where he said: Salamah bin Shabib narrated to us, Saeed bin Mansour narrated to us, Al-Harith bin Ubaid narrated to us, on the authority of Abu Imran Al-Joni, on the authority of Anas bin Malik, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “While I was sitting, Gabriel, peace be upon him, came and poked me between my shoulders. I went to a tree in which were the nests of birds. He sat in one of them, and I sat in the other. It rose and ascended until it filled the two horizons, and I turned my eyes. If I wanted to touch the sky, I could. Gabriel turned to me as if he were sitting in a squatting position, and I recognized the superiority of his knowledge of God over me. A door of the heavens was opened for me, and I saw the greatest light, and beside the veil was the fluttering of pearls and rubies. And what God willed to be revealed was revealed to me.” Then Al-Bazzar said: It is not narrated by anyone except Al-Harith bin Ubaid, and he was a famous man from the people of Basra. I said Al-Harith ibn Ubayd, this is Abu Qudamah Al-Ayadi. Muslim included him in his Sahih, except that Ibn Ma’in weakened him and said: He is nothing. Imam Ahmad said: His hadith is confused. Abu Hatim Al-Razi said: His hadith should be written down but not used as evidence. Ibn Hayyan said: He made many mistakes, so it is not permissible to use it as evidence if he is the only one who narrated it. This hadith is one of the strangest of his narrations, for it contains something strange and odd in its wording and a strange context. Perhaps it is a dream, and God knows best. Imam Ahmad said: Hajjaj told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Asim, on the authority of Abu Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in his true form, and he had six hundred wings, each of which filled the horizon, and from his wing fell pearls, rubies, and gems, of which only God knows. Ahmad is the only one who narrated it. Ahmad said: Yahya bin Adam told us, Abu Bakr bin Ayyash told us, on the authority of Idris bin Munabbih, on the authority of Wahb bin Munabbih, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, asked Gabriel to see him in his real form. He said: Call upon your Lord. So he called upon his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic, and a blackness appeared to him from the east, and it began to rise and spread. When the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw it, he was stunned. So he came to him, revived him, and wiped the spittle from his cheek. Ahmad is the only one to report this. Ibn Asakir narrated it in the biography of Utbah ibn Abi Lahab, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Ishaq, on the authority of Uthman ibn Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Hubbar ibn al-Aswad, who said: Abu Lahab and his son Utbah had prepared for the Levant, so I prepared with them. His son Utbah said: By God, I will go to Muhammad and seek refuge with him in his Lord, glory be to Him, the Most High. So he set out until he came to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, and said: O Muhammad, he disbelieves in the One who drew near, so he came close and was two bow lengths away or nearer. So the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: O God, unleash upon him one of Your dogs. Then he turned away from him and returned to his father and said: O my son, what did you say to him? So he mentioned to him what he had said, and he said: What did he say to you? He said: He said: O God, unleash one of Your dogs against him. He said: O my son, by God, his prayer is not safe for you. So we went until we reached Al-Sharaat, which was a lion colony. We went down to the monastery of a monk, and the monk said: O Arabs, what brought you to this land? Lions roam freely in it as sheep roam. Abu Lahab said to us: "You know my old age and my rights, and this man has invoked a curse against my son, and by God, I do not trust it against him. Gather your belongings to this monastery and spread out a bed for my son on it, then spread out a bed around it." So we did, and the lion came and smelled our faces. When he did not find what he wanted, he seized it and leaped up and found himself on top of the belongings. He smelled his face, then defeated him and tore his head off. Abu Lahab said: I know that he will not escape the prayer of Muhammad. God the Almighty says: {Then he was two bow lengths away or even nearer} meaning, Gabriel drew near to Muhammad when he descended to him on earth until there was between him and Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) the distance of two bow lengths, i.e., the same as if they were stretched out. This was stated by Mujahid and Qatadah. It was also said that what is meant by this is the distance between the bowstring and its middle. God the Almighty says: {or even nearer}, as we have already mentioned, that this form is used in language to confirm what is being reported and to negate what is greater than it, as in His statement: {Then your hearts hardened after that, so they are like stones or even harder} meaning, they are not softer than stones, rather they are like them or even harder and harder. Similarly, His statement: {They fear men as they fear God or even more}, and His statement: {And We sent him to a hundred thousand or more} meaning, they are not less than them, rather they are truly a hundred thousand or more. This is a confirmation of what was reported, without doubt or hesitation, as this is impossible. And so it is here, this verse, So he was two bow lengths away or even nearer. And what we said, that this approaching, close one who came between him and Muhammad, may God’s prayers and peace be upon him, was none other than Gabriel, peace be upon him, and it is the saying of the Mother of the Believers, Aisha, Ibn Masoud, Abu Dharr, and Abu Hurairah, as we will cite their hadiths soon, God willing. Muslim narrated in his Sahih on the authority of Ibn Abbas that he said: Muhammad saw his Lord twice in his heart, and he made this one of them. And it came in the hadith of Sharik bin Abi Namir on the authority of Anas in the hadith of the Isra’: Then the Compeller, the Lord of Majesty, drew near and descended. For this reason, many people have spoken about the text of this narration and mentioned strange things in it. If it is authentic, then it is attributed to another time and another story, not that it is an explanation of this verse, for this was while the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was on earth, not on the night of the Isra’. For this reason he said after it: And indeed, he saw him another time * At the Lote Tree of the Limit. So this is the night of the Isra’, and the first was on earth. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Abdul Malik bin Abi Al-Shawarib told us, Abdul Wahid bin Ziyad told us, Sulayman Al-Shaibani told us, Zur bin Hubaish told us: Abdullah bin Masoud said regarding this verse, Then he was two bow lengths away or nearer, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw Gabriel with six hundred wings. Ibn Wahb said: Ibn Lahi’ah told us, on the authority of Abu Al-Aswad, on the authority of Urwah, on the authority of Aisha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The first thing that happened to the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was that he saw Gabriel in his sleep in Ajyad. Then he went out to relieve himself, and Gabriel cried out to him: O Muhammad, O Muhammad! So the Messenger of God looked right and left, but did not see anyone, for three days. Then he raised his eyes and saw that he was the second of his two feet, one with the other, on the horizon of the sky, and he said: O Muhammad, Gabriel is calming him. So the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him) fled until he entered among the people, and he looked but did not see anything. Then he went out from the people and looked and saw him. Then he entered among the people and did not see anything. Then he went out and looked and saw him. This is the saying of God, the Almighty: "And by the star when it goes down. * Your companion has neither strayed nor erred. * Nor does he speak from [his own] inclination. * It is not but a revelation revealed. * One strong in strength taught him. * Possessor of wisdom. So he rose * And he was on the highest horizon. * Then he drew near and descended" meaning Gabriel to Muhammad, peace and blessings of God be upon them both. And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. They say: A bow length is half a finger. Some of them said: Two cubits were between them. Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb with it. And in the hadith of Az-Zuhri from Abu Salamah from Jabir, there is evidence for this. Al-Bukhari narrated from Talq ibn Ghannam from Zaidah from Ash-Shaibani, who said: I asked Zura about the statement: "And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. * Then He revealed to His Servant what He revealed." He said: Abdullah told us that Muhammad (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw Gabriel and he had six hundred wings. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Buzay` al-Baghdadi told me, Ishaq ibn Mansur told us, Isra`il told us, on the authority of Abu Ishaq, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Yazid, on the authority of Abdullah, The heart did not lie about what it saw, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel wearing a fluttering garment that filled the space between the heavens and the earth. Based on what we have mentioned, his statement, Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed, means: So Gabriel revealed to the servant of God, Muhammad, what He revealed, or: So God revealed to His servant Muhammad what He revealed through Gabriel. Both meanings are correct. It was reported on the authority of Sa`id ibn Jubayr, regarding his statement, Then He revealed to His servant what He revealed, that he said: God revealed to him, Did He not find you an orphan? “And We have raised high your fame.” Another one said: God revealed to him that Paradise is forbidden to the prophets until you enter it, and to the nations until your nation enters it. God the Almighty said: “The heart did not deny what it saw. Then do you dispute with Him about what he sees?” Muslim said: Abu Saeed Al-Ashj narrated to us, Wakee’ narrated to us, Al-A’mash narrated to us, from Ziyad bin Husayn, from Abu Al-Aaliyah, from Ibn Abbas: The heart did not deny what it saw. “And he had certainly seen Him on another occasion.” He said: He saw Him with his heart twice. Samak narrated it in the same way on the authority of Ikrimah on the authority of Ibn Abbas, similarly. Abu Salih, Al-Suddi and others said: He saw Him with his heart twice. Ibn Mas’ud and others disagreed with him. In a narration on his authority, he stated that he saw Him in general terms, but it is interpreted as being restricted to the heart. Whoever narrated it on the basis of sight has made a strange statement, because nothing authenticated about that from the Companions may God be pleased with them. Al-Baghawi said in his commentary: A group said that he saw Him with his eye, and this is the opinion of Anas, Al-Hasan and Ikrimah, but there is some doubt about it, and God knows best. Al-Tirmidhi said: Muhammad ibn Amr ibn al-Munhal ibn Safwan told us, Yahya ibn Kathir al-Anbari told us, on the authority of Salamah ibn Ja`far, on the authority of al-Hakam ibn Abaan, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Muhammad saw his Lord. I said: Didn’t God say: No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. He said: Woe to you, that is when He manifests Himself with His light, which is His light, and he saw his Lord twice. Then he said: Good and strange. He also said: Ibn Abi Omar told us, Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mujalid, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, who said: Ibn Abbas met Ka’b at Arafat and asked him about something, so he glorified God until the mountains responded to him. Ibn Abbas said: We are the sons of Hashim. Ka’b said: God divided His vision and speech between Muhammad and Moses. He spoke to Moses twice and Muhammad saw Him twice. Masruq said: I entered upon Aisha and said: Did Muhammad see his Lord? She said: You have said something that made my hair stand on end. I said: Wait a minute. Then I recited: He has certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord. She said: Where is he taking you? It is Gabriel. Whoever told you that Muhammad saw his Lord or concealed something that he was commanded to do or knew the five about which God the Most High said: Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour and sends down the rain. He has greatly slandered God. But he did see Gabriel. He only saw him in his true form twice: once at the Lote Tree of the Limit, and once in Ajyad, and he had six hundred wings that filled the horizon. Al-Nasa’i said: Ishaq bin Ibrahim told us, Muadh bin Hisham told us, my father told me, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Are you surprised that friendship was for Abraham, speech was for Moses, and vision was for Muhammad, peace be upon them? In Sahih Muslim, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I asked the Messenger of God, peace and blessings be upon him and his family: Have you seen your Lord? He said: Light, how can I see Him? In another narration: I saw a light. Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa’id al-Ashj told us, on the authority of Abu Khalid, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, who said: They said: O Messenger of God, have you seen your Lord? He said: I saw Him with my heart twice. Then he recited: The heart did not lie about what it saw. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ibn Hamid, on the authority of Mihran, on the authority of Musa bin Ubaidah, on the authority of Muhammad bin Ka’b, on the authority of some of the companions of the Prophet, peace and blessings be upon him, who said: We said: O Messenger of God, have you seen your Lord? He said: I did not see Him with my eyes, but I saw Him with my heart twice. Then he recited: Then He drew near and came closer. Then Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Hasan bin Muhammad bin Al-Sabah told us, Muhammad bin Abdullah Al-Ansari told us, Ibad bin Mansour told me: I asked Ikrimah about His statement: The heart did not lie about what it saw. Ikrimah said: Do you want me to tell you that it saw Him? I said: Yes. He said: He saw Him, then he saw Him. He said: So I asked Al-Hasan about it, and he said: He saw His glory, His greatness, and His cloak. My father told us, Muhammad bin Mujahid told us, Abu Amir Al-Aqdi told us, Abu Khaldah told us on the authority of Abu Al-Aliyah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was asked: Have you seen your Lord? He said: I saw a river and I saw behind the river a veil, and I saw behind the veil a light other than which I had never seen. This is very strange. As for the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad: Aswad ibn Amir told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I saw my Lord, the Mighty and Sublime, then it is a hadith whose chain of transmission meets the criteria of authenticity, but it is an abbreviated version of the hadith of a dream, as Imam Ahmad also narrated: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ayoub, on the authority of Abu Qilabah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “My Lord came to me last night in the most beautiful form - I think he meant in a dream - and said: O Muhammad, do you know what the highest assembly disputes about? I said: No. Then He placed His hand between my shoulders until I felt its coolness between my breasts - or he said my throat - and I knew what was in the heavens and what was on the earth. Then He said: O Muhammad, do you know what the highest assembly disputes about? I said: Yes, they dispute about…” Expiations and degrees. He said: What are the expiations? He said: I said: Staying in the mosques after the prayers, walking to the congregational prayers, and performing ablution thoroughly even in difficult situations. Whoever does that will live well and die well, and he will be free from his sins as on the day his mother bore him. And he said: Say, O Muhammad, when you pray: O God, I ask You to do good deeds, abandon evil deeds, and love the poor. And if You intend a trial for Your servants, take me to You without being tested. He said: And the degrees are giving food, spreading peace, and praying at night while people are asleep. Something similar was mentioned at the end of Surah Sad from Muadh. Ibn Jarir narrated it from another chain of transmission on the authority of Ibn Abbas, and it contains another context and a strange addition. He said: Ahmad ibn Isa al-Tamimi told me, Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Sayyar told me, my father told me on the authority of Sa`id ibn Zurbi on the authority of Umar ibn Sulayman, on the authority of Ata` on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “I saw my Lord in the most beautiful form, and He said to me: ‘O Muhammad, do you know what the highest assembly disputes about?’ I said: ‘No, O Lord.’ So He placed His hand between my shoulders, and I felt its coolness between my breasts, and I knew what was in the heavens and the earth, and I said: ‘O Lord, regarding the degrees and expiations, and moving the feet to the congregations, and waiting for the prayer after the prayer.’ I said: ‘O Lord, You took Abraham as a friend and spoke to Moses directly, and You did this and that.’ He said: ‘Did I not expand your breast for you? Did I not remove your burden from you? Did I not do to you? Did I not do to you?’ He said: ‘Then He confided in me things that I was not permitted to relate to you.’ He said: ‘This is what He said in His Book: “Then He approached and came closer, and was two bow lengths or nearer, and revealed to His Servant what He revealed.’ What…” The heart lied about what it saw. So He placed the light of my sight in my heart, so I looked at Him with my heart. Its chain of transmission is weak. Al-Hafiz Ibn Asakir mentioned with his chain of transmission back to Hubbar ibn al-Aswad may God be pleased with him that when Utbah ibn Abi Lahab went out to trade with the people of Ash-Sham, he said to the people of Makkah, Know that I am an unbeliever in the One who drew near and hung down. When his words reached the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him), he said, God has set upon him one of His dogs. Hubbar said, “So I was with them and we camped in a land with many lions. I saw a lion come and sniff the heads of the people one by one until it stepped over to Utbah and cut off his head from among them.” Ibn Ishaq and others mentioned in the Seerah that this happened in the land of Az-Zarqa’, and it was said in As-Sarat, and that he went against them that night, and that they made him stay among them and slept around him, then the lion came and began to roar, then stepped over to them and crushed his head. May God curse it. And the Almighty said: And he had already seen him in another descent * At the Lote Tree of the Limit * Near it is the Garden of Refuge. This is the second time that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in the form in which God created him, and it was on the Night of the Isra’. We have already presented the hadiths related about the Isra’ with their chains of transmission and wordings at the beginning of Surat Subhan, so there is no need to repeat them here. It was mentioned that Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, used to confirm the vision on the night of the Isra’ and he used this verse as evidence, and a group of the early and later generations followed him. However, groups of the Companions, may God be pleased with them, the Followers, and others disagreed with him. Imam Ahmad said: Hasan ibn Musa told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, on the authority of Asim ibn Bahdalah, Anzar ibn Hubaish, on the authority of Ibn Mas’ud, regarding this verse, And he had seen him on another occasion, * at the Lote Tree of the Limit, he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said, I saw Gabriel, and he had six hundred wings, from which were scattered feathers of pearls and rubies. This is a good, strong chain of transmission. Ahmad also said: Yahya ibn Adam told us, Sharik told us, on the authority of Jami’ ibn Abi Rashid, on the authority of Abi Wa’il, on the authority of Abdullah, who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in his true form, and he had six hundred wings, each of which filled the horizon, and from his wing fell…” The exaggerations of the pearls and rubies, God knows best. Its chain of transmission is also good. Imam Ahmad also said: Zaid ibn al-Hubab told us, Husayn told us, Asim ibn Bahdalah told us, he said, I heard Shaqiq ibn Salamah say: I heard Ibn Masoud say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: I saw Gabriel on the Lote Tree of the Limit and he had six hundred wings. I asked Asim about wings and he refused to tell me. He said, So some of his companions told me that a wing is the distance between the east and the west. This is also a good chain of transmission. Ahmad said: Zaid ibn al-Hubab told us, Husayn told us, Asim ibn Bahdalah told us, Shaqiq ibn Salamah told me: I heard Ibn Masoud say: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “Gabriel (peace be upon him) came to me in a green garment with pearls hanging from it.” Its chain of transmission is also good. Imam Ahmad said: Yahya told us on the authority of Ismail, Aamir told us: Masruq came to Aisha and said: O Mother of the Believers, did Muhammad (peace and blessings be upon him) see his Lord, the Almighty and Majestic? She said: Glory be to God, my hair stood on end when you said this. Where are you from three things, whoever told you about them has lied: Whoever told you that Muhammad saw his Lord has lied. Then you read: No vision can grasp Him, but He grasps all vision. “It is not for a human being that God should speak to him except by revelation or from behind a veil.” Whoever told you that He knows what will happen tomorrow has lied. Then you read: “Indeed, God has knowledge of the Hour. He sends down the rain and knows what is in the wombs.” Whoever told you that Muhammad concealed things has lied. Then you read: O Messenger, announce that which has been revealed to you from your Lord. But he saw Gabriel in his true form twice. Imam Ahmad also said: Muhammad bin Abi Uday narrated to us, on the authority of Dawud, on the authority of Al-Sha’bi, on the authority of Masruq, who said: I was with Aisha and I said: Doesn’t God say: And he certainly saw him on the clear horizon and And he certainly saw him on another occasion. She said: I am the first of this nation to ask the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, about it, and he said: That was Gabriel. He did not see him in the form in which he was created except twice. He saw him descending from the heaven to the earth, his great creation filling the space between the heaven and the earth. They included it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Al-Sha’bi with it. Narrated by Abu Dharr Imam Ahmad said: Affan told us, Hammam told us, Qatadah told us, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, who said: I said to Abu Dharr, “If you had seen the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), I would have asked him.” He said, And what would you have asked him? He said, I would have asked him, ‘Did he see his Lord?’ He said, I did ask him, ‘I saw Him as light, how could I see Him?’ This is how it appears in the narration of Imam Ahmad. Muslim narrated it through two chains of transmission with two wordings. He said: Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah told us, Waki’ told us, on the authority of Yazid bin Ibrahim, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: I asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), Did you see your Lord? He said, Light, how could I see Him. And he said: Muhammad bin Bashar told us, Muadh bin Hisham told us, my father told us, on the authority of Qatadah, on the authority of Abdullah bin Shaqiq, who said: I said to Abu Dharr, “If you had seen the Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him), I would have asked him.” He said, What would you ask him about? He said, I would have asked him, ‘Did you see your Lord?’ Abu Dharr said: I asked him and he said, I saw a light. Al-Khalal mentioned in his book, Ilal, that Imam Ahmad was asked about this hadith and he said, I have always disapproved of it and I do not know what its reason is. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Amr ibn Awn al-Wasiti told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: He saw Him with his heart, but did not see Him with his eyes. Ibn Khuzaymah tried to claim that there was an interruption in the chain of transmission between Abdullah ibn Shaqiq and Abu Dharr. As for Ibn al-Jawzi, he interpreted it as meaning that Abu Dharr might have asked the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) before the Isra’ and he answered him as he did. If he had asked him after the Isra’, he would have answered him positively. This is very weak, because Aisha, the Mother of the Believers may God be pleased with her, asked about that after the Isra’ and it was not proven that she had seen Him. Whoever says that he addressed her according to her level of intellect or tried to prove her wrong in what she believed, like Ibn Khuzaymah in the Book of Tawhid, then he is the one who is mistaken, and God knows best. An-Nasa’i said: Ya’qub ibn Ibrahim told us, Hisham told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of al-Hakam, on the authority of Yazid ibn Sharik, on the authority of Abu Dharr, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) saw his Lord with his heart, but did not see Him with his sight. It was proven in Sahih Muslim on the authority of Abu Bakr bin Abi Shaybah, on the authority of Ali bin Masahr, on the authority of Abdul Malik bin Abi Sulayman, on the authority of Ata bin Abi Rabah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him, that he said regarding the Almighty’s statement: And he had certainly seen him on another occasion, he said that he saw Gabriel, peace be upon him. Mujahid said about the statement of God, And he had already seen him on another occasion, that he said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, saw Gabriel in his original form twice. Qatadah, Ar-Rabi’ ibn Anas and others said the same. And the statement of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, When that which covers the lote-tree covers has already been mentioned in the hadiths of the Night Journey that it was covered by angels like crows, and the light of the Lord covered it, and colors covered it, I do not know what they are. And Imam Ahmad said: Malik ibn Mughul told us, Az-Zubayr ibn Adi told us, on the authority of Talhah, on the authority of Marrah, on the authority of Abdullah, who is Ibn Mas’ud, who said: When the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was taken on the Night Journey, he reached the Lote Tree of the Limit, which is in the seventh heaven. Whatever ascends from the earth ends there, and whatever descends from above it ends there, and whatever descends from above it ends there, and he is taken there. When that which covers the lote-tree covers he said: A bed of gold. He said: And the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, was given three things: He was given the five daily prayers, he was given the last verses of Surat Al-Baqarah, and forgiveness was given to those of his nation who do not associate anything with God for the sins committed. It was narrated exclusively by Muslim. Abu Ja`far al-Razi said, on the authority of al-Rabi`, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah or someone else - Abu Ja`far was unsure - who said: When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) was taken on the Night Journey al-Isra, he reached the lote-tree. It was said to him: This is the lote-tree, and the light of the Creator covered it, and the angels covered it like crows when they perch on a tree. Then he spoke to him and said: Ask. Ibn Abi Nujayh said, on the authority of Mujahid: When that which covers the lote-tree covers it He said: The branches of the lote-tree were pearls, rubies and emeralds. The Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) saw them and saw his Lord with his heart. Ibn Zayd said: It was said: O Messenger of God, what did you see covering that lote-tree? He said: I saw a moth of gold covering it, and I saw on each of its leaves an angel standing, glorifying God, the Almighty and Majestic. And the Almighty’s saying: His sight did not swerve, nor did he transgress. Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, said: He did not go right or left. And he did not transgress: He did not go beyond what he was commanded to do. This is a great characteristic of steadfastness and obedience, for he did nothing but what he was commanded to do, and he did not ask for more than what he was given. How beautiful is what the poet said: He saw the paradise of refuge and what is above it, and if anyone else had seen what he had seen, he would have been lost. And the Almighty’s saying: He has certainly seen some of the greatest signs of his Lord is like His saying: That We may show you some of Our greatest signs, meaning those that indicate Our power and greatness. And with these two verses, those of the Sunnis who believed that the vision that night did not occur were proven by saying: He has certainly seen some of the greatest signs of his Lord. And if he had seen his Lord, he would have informed about that and told that to the people. And the explanation of that has been presented in Surat Subhan. Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr told us, Muhammad ibn Talhah told us, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Qays, on the authority of Ishaq ibn Abi al-Kahtalah. Muhammad said, I think it was on the authority of Ibn Mas`ud, that he said: Muhammad did not see Gabriel in his true form except twice: Once, he asked him to show him himself in his true form, so he showed him his form and the horizon was blocked. The other time, he ascended with him when he ascended with him. And His statement: “And he was at the highest horizon. Then he drew near and came closer. And was at a distance of two bow lengths or nearer. And He revealed to His Servant what He revealed.” When Gabriel perceived his Lord, the Almighty, he returned to his true form and prostrated. So His statement: “And he had certainly seen him in another descent. At the Lote Tree of the Utmost Boundary. Near it is the Garden of Refuge. When that which covered the Lote Tree covered him. His sight did not swerve, nor did it transgress. He had certainly seen of the greatest signs of his Lord.” He said: The creation of Gabriel, peace be upon him. Ahmad narrated it in this way, but it is strange.
53:19: God the Almighty says, rebuking the polytheists for their worship of idols, rivals and statues, and for building houses for them in imitation of the Kaaba that was built by the Friend of the Most Merciful, peace be upon him: Have you seen Al-Lat? Al-Lat was a white, engraved rock, and there was a house on it in Taif, with curtains and caretakers, and around it was a courtyard that was venerated by the people of Taif, who were Thaqeef and those who followed them, and they were proud of it over all the Arab tribes after the Quraysh. Ibn Jarir said: They derived its name from the name of God, so they said Al-Lat, meaning the feminine of it. God is far above what they say. It was narrated from Ibn Abbas, Mujahid and Al-Rabi' bin Anas that they read Al-Lat with a shaddah on the ta' and they explained it as meaning that he was a man who used to mix gruel for the pilgrims in the pre-Islamic era. When he died, they devoted themselves to his grave and worshipped it. Al-Bukhari said: Muslim, he is the son of Ibrahim, told us, Abu Al-Ashab told us, Abu Al-Jawza told us, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with them both, regarding His statement: Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, he said: Al-Lat was a man who kneaded the gruel of the pilgrims. Ibn Jarir said: And so is Al-Uzza from Al-Aziz, and it was a tree with buildings and curtains in Nakhal, and it is between Mecca and Al-Taif, and the Quraysh used to venerate it, as Abu Sufyan said on the day of UHud 11:We have Al-Uzza, and you have no Uzza. So the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Say: God is our Master, and you have no Master.” Al-Bukhari narrated from the hadith of Az-Zuhri from Humayd ibn Abd al-Rahman from Abu Hurayrah who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: Whoever swears and says in his oath, ‘By al-Lat and al-‘Uzza,’ let him say, ‘There is no god but God.’ And whoever says to his companion, ‘Come, I will gamble with you,’ let him give in charity. This is attributed to someone who slipped his tongue in doing so, as their tongues were accustomed to doing in the time of ignorance, as al-Nasa’i said: Ahmad ibn Bakkar and Abd al-Hamid ibn Muhammad told us: Mukhallad told us: Yunus told us from his father: Mus’ab ibn Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas told me from his father who said: I swore by al-Lat and al-‘Uzza, and my companions said to me, ‘What a bad thing you said! You spoke nonsense.’ So I came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him, and he said, ‘Say, “There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things.” And spit to your left three times, and seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan, and then do not do it again.’” As for Manat, it was in Al-Mushallal near Qudayd, between Makkah and Madinah. During the pre-Islamic period, the Khuza'ah, the Aws, and the Khazraj tribes used to venerate it and perform Hajj from it to the Ka'bah. Al-Bukhari narrated something similar from Aishah. There were other tyrants in the Arabian Peninsula and elsewhere that the Arabs venerated as they venerated the Ka'bah, other than these three that were mentioned in His Noble Book. He only mentioned these three because they are more famous than the others. Ibn Ishaq said in Al-Seerah: The Arabs had idols alongside the Kaaba, which were houses that they venerated as they venerated the Kaaba. They had custodians and guards, and gifts were given to them as gifts are given to the Kaaba, and they circumambulated around it as they circumambulated around it, and sacrifices were made there. They knew the superiority of the Kaaba over them because they had known that it was the house of Abraham, peace be upon him, and his mosque. The Quraysh and Banu Kinanah had Al-Uzza in Nakhl, and its custodians and guards were Banu Shaiban from Sulaym, allies of Banu Hashim. I said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid ibn Al-Walid to it, and he demolished it and began to say: Oh, my God, your ingratitude is nothing but glory to You. I have seen that God has humiliated you. Al-Nasa’i said: Ali ibn al-Mundhir told us, Ibn Fadil told us, al-Walid ibn Juma’ told us, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, who said: When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) conquered Mecca, he sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to Nakhal, where al-Uzza was. Khalid came to it and it was surrounded by three palm fronds. He cut down the palm fronds and demolished the house that was on them. Then he came to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and informed him. The Prophet said: Go back, for you have done nothing. So Khalid went back. When the guards who were guarding it saw him, they resorted to tricks, saying: O Uzza, O Uzza. Khalid went to it and saw a naked woman with her hair disheveled, throwing dirt on her head. He plunged his sword into her until he killed her. Then he returned to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and informed him. He said: That is al-Uzza! Ibn Ishaq said: Al-Lat belonged to Thaqeef in Taif, and its custodians and chamberlains were Banu Mu'tab. I said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah and Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb to it, so they demolished it and built a mosque in its place in Taif. Ibn Ishaq said: Manat belonged to the Aws and Khazraj and those who followed their religion from the people of Yathrib on the sea coast in the direction of Al-Mashallal in Qadid, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb to it, so he demolished it. It is said that Ali ibn Abi Talib said: Dhu al-Khalasa belonged to Daws, Khatham, Bajila, and those who were in their land from the Arabs in Tabalah. I said: It was called the Yemeni Kaaba, and the Kaaba in Mecca was called the Levantine Kaaba. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali to it, and he demolished it. He said: It was the property of Tayy’ and those near it on Mount Tayy’, from Salma and Aja. Ibn Hisham said: Some of the people of knowledge told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali ibn Abi Talib to it, and he demolished it. He chose two swords from it: al-Rasub and al-Mukhdam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them to him as gifts, and they were the swords of Ali. Ibn Ishaq said: The Himyar and the people of Yemen had a house in Sana’a called Riyam, and it was mentioned that there was a black dog in it, and the two rabbis who went with Tubba’ extracted it, killed it, and demolished the house. Ibn Ishaq said: Rida was a house for the Banu Rabi’ah ibn Ka’b ibn Sa’d ibn Zayd Manat ibn Tamim, and Al-Mustawgir ibn Rabi’ah ibn Ka’b ibn Sa’d said about it when he demolished it in Islam: I stressed on the satisfaction of the severity of the desert, leaving it in a spacious valley Ibn Hisham said: He lived for three hundred and thirty years and he is the one who said: I am tired of life and its length, and I have lived hundreds of years One hundred years later, two hundred years later, and I lived for the number of months Is there nothing left but what we have lost, a day that passes and a night that challenges us? Ibn Ishaq said: Dhu al-Ka’bat belonged to Bakr and Taghlib, the sons of Wa’il and Iyad Basnad, and A’sha ibn Qays ibn Tha’laba said about him: Between Al-Khawranq, Al-Sudair, Barq, and the house of the Kaaba from Sindad And for this reason the Almighty said: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other? Then the Almighty said: Do you have males and He has females? That is, do you attribute to Him a son and make His son a female, and choose for yourselves males? If you and a created being like you were to divide this division, it would be an unfair division, that is, unjust and invalid. So how do you divide this division between your Lord, which, if it were between two created beings, would be unjust and foolish? And the Almighty said, denouncing them for what they innovated and invented of lying, slander, and disbelief in worshipping idols and calling them gods: They are only names which you have named, you and your fathers, that is, of your own accord. For them God has sent down no authority, that is, no proof. They follow nothing but assumption and what their souls desire. That is, they have no basis except their good opinion of their fathers who followed this false path before them, and nothing but their own share in their leadership and the glorification of their ancient fathers. And there has already come to them guidance from their Lord meaning that God sent to them messengers with the enlightening truth and the decisive proof, yet despite this they did not follow what they brought them nor did they submit to it. Then God the Almighty said: Or shall man have what he desires? That is, not everyone who desires good will get it. It is not according to your desires or the desires of the People of the Scripture. Not everyone who claims to be guided will be as they say, and not everyone who desires something will get it. Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq told us, Abu ‘Awana told us, on the authority of ‘Umar ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: When one of you makes a wish, let him consider what he desires, for he does not know what will be written for him of his wish. Ahmad was the only one to narrate it. And His statement: To God belongs the Hereafter and the first, that is, the entire matter belongs to God, the Owner of this world and the Hereafter, and the One who controls this world and the Hereafter. He is the One who wills whatever happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen. And the Almighty’s saying: And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except after God has given permission for whom He wills and is pleased with. Like His saying: Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? “And intercession does not benefit with Him except for him whom He permits.” So if this is true of the angels brought near, then how can you, you ignorant ones, hope for the intercession of these idols and rivals with God, when He, the Almighty, did not legislate their worship nor did He permit it, rather He forbade it on the tongues of all His Messengers and revealed all His books forbidding it?

This is attributed to someone who slipped his tongue in doing so, as their tongues were accustomed to doing in the time of ignorance, as al-Nasa’i said: Ahmad ibn Bakkar and Abd al-Hamid ibn Muhammad told us: Mukhallad told us: Yunus told us from his father: Mus’ab ibn Sa’d ibn Abi Waqqas told me from his father who said: I swore by al-Lat and al-‘Uzza, and my companions said to me, ‘What a bad thing you said! You spoke nonsense.’ So I came to the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) and mentioned that to him, and he said, ‘Say, “There is no god but God alone, with no partner. His is the dominion and His is the praise, and He has power over all things.” And spit to your left three times, and seek refuge in God from the accursed Satan, and then do not do it again.’” As for Manat, it was in Al-Mushallal near Qudayd, between Makkah and Madinah. During the pre-Islamic period, the Khuza'ah, the Aws, and the Khazraj tribes used to venerate it and perform Hajj from it to the Ka'bah. Al-Bukhari narrated something similar from Aishah. There were other tyrants in the Arabian Peninsula and elsewhere that the Arabs venerated as they venerated the Ka'bah, other than these three that were mentioned in His Noble Book. He only mentioned these three because they are more famous than the others. Ibn Ishaq said in Al-Seerah: The Arabs had idols alongside the Kaaba, which were houses that they venerated as they venerated the Kaaba. They had custodians and guards, and gifts were given to them as gifts are given to the Kaaba, and they circumambulated around it as they circumambulated around it, and sacrifices were made there. They knew the superiority of the Kaaba over them because they had known that it was the house of Abraham, peace be upon him, and his mosque. The Quraysh and Banu Kinanah had Al-Uzza in Nakhl, and its custodians and guards were Banu Shaiban from Sulaym, allies of Banu Hashim. I said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Khalid ibn Al-Walid to it, and he demolished it and began to say: Oh, my God, your ingratitude is nothing but glory to You. I have seen that God has humiliated you. Al-Nasa’i said: Ali ibn al-Mundhir told us, Ibn Fadil told us, al-Walid ibn Juma’ told us, on the authority of Abu al-Tufayl, who said: When the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) conquered Mecca, he sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to Nakhal, where al-Uzza was. Khalid came to it and it was surrounded by three palm fronds. He cut down the palm fronds and demolished the house that was on them. Then he came to the Prophet (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and informed him. The Prophet said: Go back, for you have done nothing. So Khalid went back. When the guards who were guarding it saw him, they resorted to tricks, saying: O Uzza, O Uzza. Khalid went to it and saw a naked woman with her hair disheveled, throwing dirt on her head. He plunged his sword into her until he killed her. Then he returned to the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) and informed him. He said: That is al-Uzza! Ibn Ishaq said: Al-Lat belonged to Thaqeef in Taif, and its custodians and chamberlains were Banu Mu'tab. I said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Al-Mughirah ibn Shu'bah and Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb to it, so they demolished it and built a mosque in its place in Taif. Ibn Ishaq said: Manat belonged to the Aws and Khazraj and those who followed their religion from the people of Yathrib on the sea coast in the direction of Al-Mashallal in Qadid, so the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) sent Abu Sufyan Sakhr ibn Harb to it, so he demolished it. It is said that Ali ibn Abi Talib said: Dhu al-Khalasa belonged to Daws, Khatham, Bajila, and those who were in their land from the Arabs in Tabalah. I said: It was called the Yemeni Kaaba, and the Kaaba in Mecca was called the Levantine Kaaba. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali to it, and he demolished it. He said: It was the property of Tayy’ and those near it on Mount Tayy’, from Salma and Aja. Ibn Hisham said: Some of the people of knowledge told me that the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, sent Ali ibn Abi Talib to it, and he demolished it. He chose two swords from it: al-Rasub and al-Mukhdam. The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, gave them to him as gifts, and they were the swords of Ali. Ibn Ishaq said: The Himyar and the people of Yemen had a house in Sana’a called Riyam, and it was mentioned that there was a black dog in it, and the two rabbis who went with Tubba’ extracted it, killed it, and demolished the house. Ibn Ishaq said: Rida was a house for the Banu Rabi’ah ibn Ka’b ibn Sa’d ibn Zayd Manat ibn Tamim, and Al-Mustawgir ibn Rabi’ah ibn Ka’b ibn Sa’d said about it when he demolished it in Islam: I stressed on the satisfaction of the severity of the desert, leaving it in a spacious valley Ibn Hisham said: He lived for three hundred and thirty years and he is the one who said: I am tired of life and its length, and I have lived hundreds of years One hundred years later, two hundred years later, and I lived for the number of months Is there nothing left but what we have lost, a day that passes and a night that challenges us? Ibn Ishaq said: Dhu al-Ka’bat belonged to Bakr and Taghlib, the sons of Wa’il and Iyad Basnad, and A’sha ibn Qays ibn Tha’laba said about him: Between Al-Khawranq, Al-Sudair, Barq, and the house of the Kaaba from Sindad And for this reason the Almighty said: Have you considered Al-Lat and Al-Uzza, and Manat, the third, the other? Then the Almighty said: Do you have males and He has females? That is, do you attribute to Him a son and make His son a female, and choose for yourselves males? If you and a created being like you were to divide this division, it would be an unfair division, that is, unjust and invalid. So how do you divide this division between your Lord, which, if it were between two created beings, would be unjust and foolish? And the Almighty said, denouncing them for what they innovated and invented of lying, slander, and disbelief in worshipping idols and calling them gods: They are only names which you have named, you and your fathers, that is, of your own accord. For them God has sent down no authority, that is, no proof. They follow nothing but assumption and what their souls desire. That is, they have no basis except their good opinion of their fathers who followed this false path before them, and nothing but their own share in their leadership and the glorification of their ancient fathers. And there has already come to them guidance from their Lord meaning that God sent to them messengers with the enlightening truth and the decisive proof, yet despite this they did not follow what they brought them nor did they submit to it. Then God the Almighty said: Or shall man have what he desires? That is, not everyone who desires good will get it. It is not according to your desires or the desires of the People of the Scripture. Not everyone who claims to be guided will be as they say, and not everyone who desires something will get it. Imam Ahmad said: Ishaq told us, Abu ‘Awana told us, on the authority of ‘Umar ibn Abi Salamah, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: When one of you makes a wish, let him consider what he desires, for he does not know what will be written for him of his wish. Ahmad was the only one to narrate it. And His statement: To God belongs the Hereafter and the first, that is, the entire matter belongs to God, the Owner of this world and the Hereafter, and the One who controls this world and the Hereafter. He is the One who wills whatever happens, and whatever He does not will does not happen. And the Almighty’s saying: And how many an angel is there in the heavens whose intercession will not avail at all except after God has given permission for whom He wills and is pleased with. Like His saying: Who is he that can intercede with Him except by His permission? “And intercession does not benefit with Him except for him whom He permits.” So if this is true of the angels brought near, then how can you, you ignorant ones, hope for the intercession of these idols and rivals with God, when He, the Almighty, did not legislate their worship nor did He permit it, rather He forbade it on the tongues of all His Messengers and revealed all His books forbidding it?
53:27: God the Almighty says, denouncing the polytheists for calling the angels female, and making them daughters of God. God is exalted above that, as He the Almighty says: “And they have made the angels, who are the servants of the Most Merciful, females. Did they witness their creation? Their testimony will be recorded, and they will be questioned.” For this reason God the Almighty says: And they have no knowledge thereof, meaning they have no correct knowledge to confirm what they said. Rather, it is a lie, a forgery, a fabrication, and a heinous disbelief. They follow nothing but conjecture, and conjecture avails nothing against the truth, meaning it is of no use and can never take the place of the truth. It has been proven in the Sahih that the Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: Beware of conjecture, for conjecture is the most false of speech. God the Almighty says: {So turn away from he who turns away from Our remembrance} meaning, turn away from the one who turns away from the truth and abandons it. God the Almighty says: {and desires nothing but the life of this world} meaning, his main concern and the extent of his knowledge is this world, so that is the ultimate goal of what is no good. For this reason, God the Almighty said: {That is the extent of their knowledge} meaning, seeking this world and striving for it is the ultimate goal they have reached. Imam Ahmad narrated on the authority of the Mother of the Believers, Aisha may God be pleased with her, that she said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) said: This world is the home of he who has no home, and the wealth of he who has no wealth, and he who has no mind gathers for it. In the well-known supplication, it is said: O God, do not make this world our greatest concern or the extent of our deeds. God the Almighty says: {Indeed, your Lord is most knowing of who has strayed from His way, and He is most knowing of who is guided} meaning, He is the Creator of all creation and the One who knows what is in the best interests of His servants. He is the One who guides whom He wills and misguides whom He wills. All of this is due to His power, knowledge, and wisdom. He is the Just One who never transgresses, neither in His law nor in His power.

53:31: God Almighty tells us that He is the Owner of the heavens and the earth, and that He is independent of anything other than Him, the Ruler of His creation with justice and the Creator of creation with truth, That He may reward those who do evil for what they have done and reward those who do good with goodness. That is, He rewards each person for his work, if good then good and if evil then evil. Then He explained the doers of good as being those who avoid major sins and immoralities, that is, they do not engage in major forbidden sins, and if some minor sins occur from them, He will forgive them and conceal them, as He said in the other verse, If you avoid the major sins you are forbidden, We will remove from you your lesser sins and admit you to a noble entrance. And He said here, Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except for minor sins. This is an isolated exception, because minor sins are among the minor sins and insignificant deeds. Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I have never seen anything more resembling a lick than what Abu Hurayrah said, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty has decreed for the son of Adam his share of adultery, which he will inevitably attain. The adultery of the eye is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speaking, the soul desires and longs, and the private parts confirm that or deny it.” They both included it in their Sahihs on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, Ibn Thawr told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha that Ibn Mas'ud said: The adultery of the eyes is looking, the adultery of the lips is kissing, the adultery of the hands is touching, and the adultery of the feet is walking. The private parts confirm or deny that. If he comes forward with his private parts, then he has committed adultery, otherwise it is a small touch. Masruq and al-Sha'bi said the same. Abd al-Rahman ibn Nafi', who was called Ibn Lubabah at-Ta'ifi, said: I asked Abu Hurayrah about the statement of God: "Except a small touch." He said: The kiss, the wink, the look, and direct contact. So if circumcised parts touch circumcised parts, then ritual ablution is required, and that is adultery. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "Except a small touch," except what came before. Zayd ibn Aslam said the same. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said regarding this verse: Except for the one who touches: He said: The one who touches the sin and then abandons it. The poet said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive many. Which of your servants has not suffered? Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: Except for a touch, he said: A man touches a sin and then abandons it. He said: The people of the Age of Ignorance used to circumambulate the House and they would say: If you forgive, O God, you forgive many. Which of your servants has not suffered? Ibn Jarir and others narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Jarir said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me, Abu Asim told us, Zakariya ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Those who avoid major sins and immoralities, except minor ones. He said: It is the man who commits an immoral act and then repents. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive many. Which of your servants has not suffered? Thus, Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Uthman Abu Uthman Al-Basri on the authority of Abu Asim Al-Nabil. Then he said: This is a saheeh hasan ghareeb hadeeth which we do not know of except from the hadeeth of Zakariya bin Ishaq. Al-Bazzar said the same: We do not know of it being narrated in a connected chain of transmission except from this source. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Baghawi included it on the authority of Abu Asim Al-Nabil. Al-Baghawi only mentioned it in his commentary on Surat At-Tanzil, but there is some doubt about its authenticity as a marfu’ hadeeth. Then Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzigh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him. I think he narrated it as a marfu’ hadeeth in the verse: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except for minor sins, he said: Minor sins include adultery, then he repents and does not return to it. And the slightest of theft, then he repents and does not return to it, and the slightest of drinking alcohol, then he repents and does not return to it. He said: That is the slightest of the things. Ibn Bashar told us, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the words of God Almighty: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except for the slightest of them, he said: The slightest of the things, such as adultery, theft, or drinking alcohol, then he does not return to it. Yaqub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor sins, he said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: It is the man who commits a minor sin such as adultery or drinking alcohol, so he avoids it and repents from it. Ibn Jarir said, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except minor sins means he commits it immediately. I said: Adultery? He said: Adultery then he repents. Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The minor sin is the one who commits a minor sin. Al-Suddi said: Abu Saleh said: I was asked about Al-Lam’am and I said: It is a man who commits a sin then repents. I informed Ibn Abbas of that and he said: A noble angel has helped you with it. Al-Baghawi narrated it. Ibn Jarir narrated from Al-Muthanna bin Al-Sabah - and he is weak - from Amr bin Shuaib that Abdullah bin Amr said: Al-Lam’am is anything less than shirk. Sufyan Al-Thawri said from Jabir Al-Ju’fi from Ata’ from Ibn Al-Zubayr: Except for Al-Lam’am He said: It is what is between the two limits, the limit of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. Shu’bah narrated it likewise from Al-Hakam from Ibn Abbas, similarly. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Except for Al-Lam’am Everything between the two limits, the limit of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, which is expiated by prayers, is Al-Lam’am, and it is less than everything that is obligatory. As for the limit of this world, it is every limit for which God has imposed punishment in this world. As for the limit of the Hereafter, it is everything that God has sealed with Hell and postponed its punishment until the Hereafter. This is what Ikrimah, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said. God the Almighty says: Indeed, your Lord is Vast in forgiveness, meaning His mercy encompasses all things, and His forgiveness encompasses all sins for whoever repents from them, as in His saying: “Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.’” And His saying: He is most knowing of you when He produced you from the earth, meaning He is All-Seeing of you, All-Knowing of your conditions, actions, and words that will come from you and occur from you when He produced your father from the earth, and extracted his offspring from his loins like ants, then divided them into two groups: one group for Paradise and one group for the Blaze. Likewise, His saying: And when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers, the angel to whom He is entrusted wrote down his provision, his life span, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or blessed. Makhool said: We were fetuses in our mothers' wombs, then some of us miscarried. We were among those who remained, then we were wet nurses, then some of us perished. We were among those who remained, then we became youths, then some of us perished. We were among those who remained, then we became young men, then some of us perished. We were among those who remained, then we became old men. I don't care, so what more can we expect after this? Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on his authority. God the Almighty said: So do not claim yourselves to be pure meaning do not praise yourselves, thank yourself, or express hope through your deeds. He is most knowing of who fears Him as God the Almighty said: Have you not seen those who claim themselves to be pure? Rather, God purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged, not a thread. Muslim said in his Sahih: Amr al-Naqid told us, Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, al-Layth told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, who said: I named my daughter Barra, and Zainab bint Abi Salamah said to me: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade this name, so I named her Barra. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Do not claim yourselves to be pure. Indeed, God knows best who the righteous among you are.” They said: What should we name her? He said: Name her Zainab. It has also been proven in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, where he said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Khalid al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra, on the authority of his father, who said: A man praised a man in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to you, you have cut off the neck of your companion - repeatedly. If one of you must praise his companion, then let him say: “I think so-and-so is such-and-such, and God is his judge, and I do not vouch for anyone before God. I think he is such-and-such,” if he knew that. Then he narrated it on the authority of Ghundar, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Khalid al-Hadha’ with it. And likewise, al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, and Ibn Majah narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Khalid al-Hadha’ with it. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ and Abdur-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam ibn al-Harith, who said: A man came to Uthman and praised him to his face. Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad began throwing dirt in his face and saying: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded us, when we meet flatterers, to throw dirt in their faces. Muslim and Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of al-Thawri on the authority of Mansur.
