Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of Ibn Tawus, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: I have never seen anything more resembling a lick than what Abu Hurayrah said, on the authority of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, who said: “God Almighty has decreed for the son of Adam his share of adultery, which he will inevitably attain. The adultery of the eye is looking, the adultery of the tongue is speaking, the soul desires and longs, and the private parts confirm that or deny it.” They both included it in their Sahihs on the authority of Abd al-Razzaq. Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Abd al-A'la told us, Ibn Thawr told us, Muammar told us, on the authority of al-A'mash, on the authority of Abu al-Dhaha that Ibn Mas'ud said: The adultery of the eyes is looking, the adultery of the lips is kissing, the adultery of the hands is touching, and the adultery of the feet is walking. The private parts confirm or deny that. If he comes forward with his private parts, then he has committed adultery, otherwise it is a small touch. Masruq and al-Sha'bi said the same. Abd al-Rahman ibn Nafi', who was called Ibn Lubabah at-Ta'ifi, said: I asked Abu Hurayrah about the statement of God: "Except a small touch." He said: The kiss, the wink, the look, and direct contact. So if circumcised parts touch circumcised parts, then ritual ablution is required, and that is adultery. Ali ibn Abi Talhah said on the authority of Ibn Abbas: "Except a small touch," except what came before. Zayd ibn Aslam said the same. Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Al-Muthanna told us, Muhammad Ibn Ja`far told us, Shu`bah told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, that he said regarding this verse: Except for the one who touches: He said: The one who touches the sin and then abandons it. The poet said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive many. Which of your servants has not suffered? Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Hamid told us, Jarir told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Mujahid, regarding the statement of God Almighty: Except for a touch, he said: A man touches a sin and then abandons it. He said: The people of the Age of Ignorance used to circumambulate the House and they would say: If you forgive, O God, you forgive many. Which of your servants has not suffered? Ibn Jarir and others narrated it with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet. Ibn Jarir said: Sulayman ibn Abd al-Jabbar told me, Abu Asim told us, Zakariya ibn Ishaq told us, on the authority of Amr ibn Dinar, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Those who avoid major sins and immoralities, except minor ones. He said: It is the man who commits an immoral act and then repents. He said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: If you forgive, O God, you forgive many. Which of your servants has not suffered? Thus, Al-Tirmidhi narrated it on the authority of Ahmad bin Uthman Abu Uthman Al-Basri on the authority of Abu Asim Al-Nabil. Then he said: This is a saheeh hasan ghareeb hadeeth which we do not know of except from the hadeeth of Zakariya bin Ishaq. Al-Bazzar said the same: We do not know of it being narrated in a connected chain of transmission except from this source. Ibn Abi Hatim and Al-Baghawi included it on the authority of Abu Asim Al-Nabil. Al-Baghawi only mentioned it in his commentary on Surat At-Tanzil, but there is some doubt about its authenticity as a marfu’ hadeeth. Then Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad bin Abdullah bin Buzigh told us, Yazid bin Zari’ told us, Yunus told us, on the authority of Al-Hasan, on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, may God be pleased with him. I think he narrated it as a marfu’ hadeeth in the verse: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except for minor sins, he said: Minor sins include adultery, then he repents and does not return to it. And the slightest of theft, then he repents and does not return to it, and the slightest of drinking alcohol, then he repents and does not return to it. He said: That is the slightest of the things. Ibn Bashar told us, Ibn Abi Uday told us, on the authority of Awf, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the words of God Almighty: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except for the slightest of them, he said: The slightest of the things, such as adultery, theft, or drinking alcohol, then he does not return to it. Yaqub told me, Ibn Ulayyah told us, on the authority of Abu Raja’, on the authority of Al-Hasan, regarding the statement of God: Those who avoid the major sins and immoralities, except minor sins, he said: The companions of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, used to say: It is the man who commits a minor sin such as adultery or drinking alcohol, so he avoids it and repents from it. Ibn Jarir said, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas: Except minor sins means he commits it immediately. I said: Adultery? He said: Adultery then he repents. Ibn Jarir also said: Abu Kurayb told us, Ibn Uyaynah told us, on the authority of Amr, on the authority of Ata’, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with him, who said: The minor sin is the one who commits a minor sin. Al-Suddi said: Abu Saleh said: I was asked about Al-Lam’am and I said: It is a man who commits a sin then repents. I informed Ibn Abbas of that and he said: A noble angel has helped you with it. Al-Baghawi narrated it. Ibn Jarir narrated from Al-Muthanna bin Al-Sabah - and he is weak - from Amr bin Shuaib that Abdullah bin Amr said: Al-Lam’am is anything less than shirk. Sufyan Al-Thawri said from Jabir Al-Ju’fi from Ata’ from Ibn Al-Zubayr: Except for Al-Lam’am He said: It is what is between the two limits, the limit of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter. Shu’bah narrated it likewise from Al-Hakam from Ibn Abbas, similarly. Al-Awfi said from Ibn Abbas regarding His statement: Except for Al-Lam’am Everything between the two limits, the limit of this world and the punishment of the Hereafter, which is expiated by prayers, is Al-Lam’am, and it is less than everything that is obligatory. As for the limit of this world, it is every limit for which God has imposed punishment in this world. As for the limit of the Hereafter, it is everything that God has sealed with Hell and postponed its punishment until the Hereafter. This is what Ikrimah, Qatadah and Ad-Dahhak said. God the Almighty says: Indeed, your Lord is Vast in forgiveness, meaning His mercy encompasses all things, and His forgiveness encompasses all sins for whoever repents from them, as in His saying: “Say, ‘O My servants who have transgressed against themselves, do not despair of the mercy of God. Indeed, God forgives all sins. Indeed, it is He who is the Forgiving, the Merciful.’” And His saying: He is most knowing of you when He produced you from the earth, meaning He is All-Seeing of you, All-Knowing of your conditions, actions, and words that will come from you and occur from you when He produced your father from the earth, and extracted his offspring from his loins like ants, then divided them into two groups: one group for Paradise and one group for the Blaze. Likewise, His saying: And when you were fetuses in the wombs of your mothers, the angel to whom He is entrusted wrote down his provision, his life span, his deeds, and whether he will be wretched or blessed. Makhool said: We were fetuses in our mothers' wombs, then some of us miscarried. We were among those who remained, then we were wet nurses, then some of us perished. We were among those who remained, then we became youths, then some of us perished. We were among those who remained, then we became young men, then some of us perished. We were among those who remained, then we became old men. I don't care, so what more can we expect after this? Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim on his authority. God the Almighty said: So do not claim yourselves to be pure meaning do not praise yourselves, thank yourself, or express hope through your deeds. He is most knowing of who fears Him as God the Almighty said: Have you not seen those who claim themselves to be pure? Rather, God purifies whom He wills, and they will not be wronged, not a thread. Muslim said in his Sahih: Amr al-Naqid told us, Hashim ibn al-Qasim told us, al-Layth told us, on the authority of Yazid ibn Abi Habib, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Ata’, who said: I named my daughter Barra, and Zainab bint Abi Salamah said to me: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) forbade this name, so I named her Barra. The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) said: “Do not claim yourselves to be pure. Indeed, God knows best who the righteous among you are.” They said: What should we name her? He said: Name her Zainab. It has also been proven in the hadith narrated by Imam Ahmad, where he said: Affan told us, Wahib told us, Khalid al-Hadha’ told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi Bakra, on the authority of his father, who said: A man praised a man in the presence of the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, so the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Woe to you, you have cut off the neck of your companion - repeatedly. If one of you must praise his companion, then let him say: “I think so-and-so is such-and-such, and God is his judge, and I do not vouch for anyone before God. I think he is such-and-such,” if he knew that. Then he narrated it on the authority of Ghundar, on the authority of Shu’bah, on the authority of Khalid al-Hadha’ with it. And likewise, al-Bukhari, Muslim, Abu Dawud, and Ibn Majah narrated it through various chains of narration on the authority of Khalid al-Hadha’ with it. Imam Ahmad said: Wakee’ and Abdur-Rahman told us: Sufyan told us, on the authority of Mansur, on the authority of Ibrahim, on the authority of Hammam ibn al-Harith, who said: A man came to Uthman and praised him to his face. Al-Miqdad ibn al-Aswad began throwing dirt in his face and saying: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) commanded us, when we meet flatterers, to throw dirt in their faces. Muslim and Abu Dawud narrated it on the authority of al-Thawri on the authority of Mansur.
53:33: God the Almighty says, blaming those who turn away from obeying God: He neither believed nor prayed, but lied and turned away. “And gave a little and ceased.” Ibn Abbas said: He obeyed a little then stopped. This is what Mujahid, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Ikrimah, Qatadah, and others said. Ikrimah and Sa'id said: It is like the example of people who are digging a well and while digging they find a rock that prevents them from completing the work, so they say, We ceased, and they abandon the work. God the Almighty said: Does he have knowledge of the unseen so that he sees? That is, does this one who has withheld his hand for fear of spending and having his good deeds cut off have knowledge of the unseen that what he has in his hand will be used up, so that he has withheld his good deeds so that he sees that with his own eyes? That is, the matter is not like that. Rather, he withheld charity, good deeds, righteousness, and kinship out of miserliness, stinginess, and fear. For this reason it was stated in the hadith: Spend, Bilal, and do not fear any reduction from the Lord of the Throne. God the Almighty said: And whatever you spend - He will replace it, and He is the Best of providers. God the Almighty said: Or has he not been informed of what is in the scriptures of Moses * and of Abraham, who fulfilled? Sa’id ibn Jubayr and Ath-Thawri said: That is, he conveyed all that he was commanded to do. Ibn Abbas said: He fulfilled to God by conveying. Sa’id ibn Jubayr said: He fulfilled what he was commanded to do. Qatada said: He fulfilled by obeying God and conveying His message to His creation. This statement is the preferred one by Ibn Jarir, and it includes the one before it and is supported by the statement of God the Almighty: And when Abraham was tested by his Lord with certain commands, and he fulfilled them, He said, ‘Indeed, I will make you a leader for the people.’ So he fulfilled all the commands and abandoned all the prohibitions and conveyed the message in full and perfect form. With this, he deserved to be a leader for the people to follow in all his circumstances, words and actions. God the Almighty said: Then We revealed to you, [O Muhammad], ‘Follow the religion of Abraham, inclining toward truth, and he was not of those who associate others with God.’ Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Auf al-Himsi told us, Adam ibn Abi Iyas al-Asqalani told us, Hammad ibn Salamah told us, Ja’far ibn al-Zubayr told us, on the authority of al-Qasim, on the authority of Abu Umamah, who said: The Messenger of God (blessings and peace of God be upon him) recited this verse: And Abraham who fulfilled. He said: Do you know what he fulfilled? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: And he completed his day’s deeds with four rak’ahs at the beginning of the day. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ja’far ibn al-Zubayr, and it is weak. Al-Tirmidhi said in his Jami’: Abu Ja’far al-Samnani told us, Abu Mashair told us, Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ and Abu Dharr, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of God the Almighty, that He said: O son of Adam, bow down to Me four rak’ahs at the beginning of the day and I will suffice you for the rest of it. Ibn Abi Hatim, may God have mercy on him, said: My father told us, al-Rabi’ ibn Sulayman told us, Asad ibn Musa told us, Ibn Lahi’ah told us, Zaban ibn Fa’id told us, on the authority of Sahl ibn Mu’adh ibn Anas, on the authority of his father, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, that he said: “Shall I not tell you why God, the Almighty, called Abraham His faithful friend? Indeed, he used to say every morning and evening: ‘Glory be to God when you reach the evening and when you reach the morning,’ until he finished the verse.” And Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Abu Kurayb on the authority of Rashdin bin Saad on the authority of Zaban on his authority. Then the Almighty began to explain what He had revealed in the scriptures of Abraham and Moses, saying: No soul shall bear the burden of another meaning every soul that wronged itself through disbelief or any of the sins, then it is only its own burden that no one shall bear for it, as He said: And if a heavily laden soul calls to bear its burden, nothing of it shall be borne by him, even if he were a close relative “And that man shall have nothing but what he strives for” meaning just as no one else’s burden shall be borne by him, likewise no reward shall be obtained except what he has earned for himself. From this noble verse, al-Shafi’i, may God have mercy on him, and those who followed him deduced that the reward for reading does not reach the dead, because it is not from their work or their earnings. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not urge his nation to do it, nor did he urge them to do it, nor did he guide them to it by text or allusion. This was not transmitted from any of the Companions, may God be pleased with them. If it were good, they would have preceded us to it. The chapter on acts of worship is limited to texts and is not dealt with by various types of analogies and opinions. As for… Supplication and charity are agreed upon to be valid and stipulated by the Lawgiver. As for the hadith narrated by Muslim in his Sahih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: a righteous child who prays for him, an ongoing charity after his death, or beneficial knowledge.” These three are in fact from his efforts, toil, and work, as stated in the hadith: The best of what a man eats is from what he has earned, and his child is from what he has earned. An ongoing charity, such as a waqf endowment and the like, is from the effects of his work and endowment. God the Almighty said: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have put forth and what they left behind. The knowledge that a person disseminated among the people, which people followed after him, is also from his efforts and work. It is proven in the Sahih: Whoever calls others to guidance will have a reward like that of those who follow him, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. And the Almighty’s saying: And that his effort will be seen meaning on the Day of Resurrection, like His saying: “And say, ‘Work, and God will see your work, and so will His Messenger and the believers. And you will be returned to the Knower of the unseen and the witnessed, and He will inform you of what you used to do.” That is, He will inform you of it and reward you for it with the most complete reward, if good then good, and if evil then evil. And thus He said here: Then He will reward him with the fullest reward, meaning the most abundant.

He said: Do you know what he fulfilled? I said: God and His Messenger know best. He said: And he completed his day’s deeds with four rak’ahs at the beginning of the day. Ibn Jarir narrated it on the authority of Ja’far ibn al-Zubayr, and it is weak. Al-Tirmidhi said in his Jami’: Abu Ja’far al-Samnani told us, Abu Mashair told us, Ismail ibn Ayyash told us, on the authority of Yahya ibn Sa’d, on the authority of Khalid ibn Ma’dan, on the authority of Jubayr ibn Nufayr, on the authority of Abu al-Darda’ and Abu Dharr, on the authority of the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, on the authority of God the Almighty, that He said: O son of Adam, bow down to Me four rak’ahs at the beginning of the day and I will suffice you for the rest of it. For this reason, the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, did not urge his nation to do it, nor did he urge them to do it, nor did he guide them to it by text or allusion. This was not transmitted from any of the Companions, may God be pleased with them. If it were good, they would have preceded us to it. The chapter on acts of worship is limited to texts and is not dealt with by various types of analogies and opinions. As for… Supplication and charity are agreed upon to be valid and stipulated by the Lawgiver. As for the hadith narrated by Muslim in his Sahih on the authority of Abu Hurairah, who said: The Messenger of God (peace and blessings be upon him) said: “When a person dies, his deeds come to an end except for three: a righteous child who prays for him, an ongoing charity after his death, or beneficial knowledge.” These three are in fact from his efforts, toil, and work, as stated in the hadith: The best of what a man eats is from what he has earned, and his child is from what he has earned. An ongoing charity, such as a waqf endowment and the like, is from the effects of his work and endowment. God the Almighty said: Indeed, it is We who bring the dead to life, and We record what they have put forth and what they left behind. The knowledge that a person disseminated among the people, which people followed after him, is also from his efforts and work. It is proven in the Sahih: Whoever calls others to guidance will have a reward like that of those who follow him, without that detracting from their reward in the slightest. And the Almighty’s saying: And that his effort will be seen meaning on the Day of Resurrection, like His saying: “And say, ‘Work, and God will see your work, and so will His Messenger and the believers. 53:42: God the Almighty says: And that to your Lord is the final destination, meaning the return on the Day of Resurrection. Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, Suwaid bin Saeed told us, Muslim bin Khalid told us, on the authority of Abd al-Rahman bin Sabit, on the authority of Amr bin Maymun al-Awdi, who said: Muadh bin Jabal stood up among us and said: O my sons, I am the Messenger of God (peace and blessings of God be upon him) to you. Do you know that the return to God is either to Paradise or to Hell? Al-Baghawi mentioned from the narration of Abu Ja`far al-Razi, on the authority of al-Rabi` bin Anas, on the authority of Abu al-`Aliyah, on the authority of Ubayy bin Ka`b, on the authority of the Prophet (peace and blessings of God be upon him), regarding his statement: And that to your Lord is the final destination, he said: There is no thought about the Lord. Al-Baghawi said: This is like what was narrated on the authority of Abu Hurayrah, with a chain of transmission traceable to the Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace: Think about creation and do not think about the Creator, for He is beyond thought. He also cited it, but it is not preserved with this wording. Rather, what is in the Sahih is: “Satan comes to one of you and says: Who created such-and-such? Who created such-and-such?” until he says: Who created your Lord? When one of you reaches that point, let him seek refuge in God and stop.” And in the other hadith in the Sunan: Think about the creations of God and do not think about the essence of God Almighty, for God created an angel between whose earlobe and shoulder is a journey of three hundred years, or something like that. And the words of God Almighty: And that it is He who makes laugh and weep, meaning He created laughter and crying in His servants and their cause, and they are different. And that it is He who causes death and life, like His words: Who created death and life, “And that He created the two mates, the male and female, * From a sperm-drop when it is emitted,” like His words: Does man think that he will be left neglected? * Was he not a sperm-drop of emitted semen? * Then he was a clinging clot, then He created and proportioned. * Then He made from it two mates, the male and the female. * Is not He able to give life to the dead? And the saying of God the Most High: {And that upon Him is the other creation} meaning, just as He created the beginning, He is able to restore, which is the other creation on the Day of Resurrection. {And that He is the Most Enriched and the Most Sufficient} meaning, He gave His servants wealth and made it their property, remaining with them, so that they do not need to sell it. This is the completion of His blessing upon them. Many commentators have their opinions based on this, including Abu Salih, Ibn Jarir, and others. Mujahid said: Enriched means master and Sufficient means served. Qatadah said the same. Ibn Abbas and Mujahid also said: Enriched means gave and Sufficient means pleased. It was said that its meaning is that He enriched Himself and made all creation poorer to Him. This was said by Al-Hadrami bin Lahiq. It was also said: He enriched whomever He wished of His creation, and Sufficient means He made whomever He wished of them. Ibn Zayd said: Ibn Jarir narrated both of them, but they are far apart in terms of wording. And His statement: And that He is the Lord of Sirius, Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah, Ibn Zayd, and others said: It is this blazing star called Mirzam al-Jiwa’, which a group of Arabs used to worship. And that He destroyed the former ‘Aad, who were the people of Hud, and they were called ‘Aad bin Iram bin Sam bin Noah, as God Almighty said: Have you not seen how your Lord dealt with ‘Aad, Iram, of the lofty pillars, the like of which had never been created in the land? They were among the most severe, strongest, and most rebellious of people against God Almighty and His Messenger, so God destroyed them with a furious, violent wind, which He subjected to them for seven nights and eight days in succession, meaning consecutively. God the Almighty said: {And Thamud - and what He left behind} meaning He destroyed them, leaving not a single one of them, {and the people of Noah before them} meaning before these people, {Indeed, they were more unjust and more rebellious} meaning more rebellious than those who came after them, {and the overturned cities - He turned them upside down on them, turning them upside down, and rained down upon them stones of layered baked clay. That is why He said: {and covered them with that which covered them} meaning of the stones that He sent down upon them, {and We rained down upon them a rain - how evil was the rain of those who were warned}. Qatadah said: There were four million people in the cities of Lot, and the valley was engulfed in fire, oil, and pitch, like the mouth of a furnace. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it on the authority of his father, on the authority of Muhammad ibn Wahb ibn Atiyyah, on the authority of al-Walid ibn Muslim, on the authority of Khalid, on his authority, with this word. It is very strange, {And which of the favors of your Lord do you dispute?} meaning which of the favors of God upon you, O human, do you doubt? 53:56: This is a warner meaning Muhammad, peace and blessings be upon him, of the first warners meaning of their kind, sent as they were sent, as God Almighty said: Say, 'I am not an innovation among the messengers.' "The approaching event has drawn near meaning the Resurrection has drawn near, and there is none to avert it besides God" meaning no one can repel it besides God, and no one has knowledge of it but Him. The warner is one who is cautious of the evil that he sees and fears will befall those he warns, as He said: "Except as a warner to you before a severe punishment." And in the hadith: "I am the naked warner" meaning the one who was too hastened by the severity of the evil that he saw to cover anything up, but rather he hastened to warn his people before that, so he came to them naked and hastening, and this is appropriate to His saying: "The approaching event has drawn near" meaning the Day of Resurrection has drawn near, meaning the Day of Resurrection. As he said at the beginning of the surah after it: The Hour has drawn near. Imam Ahmad said: Anas ibn ‘Ayadh told us, Abu Hatim told me - I know only from Sahl ibn Sa’d - who said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: “Beware of minor sins, for the example of minor sins is like that of people who camped in the bottom of a valley. One of them brought a stick and another brought a stick until they cooked their bread. And when the one who commits minor sins is caught by them, they will destroy him.” Abu Hazim said: The Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: Abu Nadrah said: I know only from Sahl ibn Sa’d, who said: My example and the Hour are like these two, and he separated his middle finger and the one next to the thumb, then he said: My example and the Hour are like two racehorses. Then he said: My example and the Hour are like a man sent by his people as a vanguard, and when he feared that he would be outpaced, he waved his garment, ‘You have come, you have come.’ Then the Messenger of God, may God bless him and grant him peace, said: I am that. And there are corroborating reports from other sources from the Sahih and Hasan hadiths. Then the Almighty said, denouncing the polytheists for listening to the Qur’an and turning away from it and being distracted: You are amazed that it is true, and you laugh at it in mockery and ridicule, and you do not cry, that is, as those who believe in it do, as He has informed us about them, and they fall upon their chins weeping, and it increases them in humble submission. And the Almighty said: "And you are steadfast." Sufyan al-Thawri said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: Singing is a Yemeni word, "Sing for us, sing for us." And this is what Ikrimah said. And in a narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, "Singing means turning away." And this is what Mujahid and Ikrimah said. Al-Hasan said, "Heedless." And this is a narration on the authority of the Commander of the Faithful, Ali ibn Abi Talib. And in a narration on the authority of Ibn Abbas, "You are arrogant." And al-Suddi said the same. Then the Almighty said, commanding His servants to prostrate to Him, to worship, to follow the example of His Messenger, may God bless him and grant him peace, and to worship Him alone and to be sincere. "So prostrate to God and worship," meaning, submit to Him, be sincere and unify Him alone. Al-Bukhari said: Abu Muammar narrated to us, Abdul-Warith narrated to us, Ayoub narrated to us, on the authority of Ikrimah, on the authority of Ibn Abbas, who said: The Prophet, may God bless him and grant him peace, prostrated at the star, and the Muslims, the polytheists, the jinn, and mankind prostrated with him. It was narrated by him alone, without Muslim.
